title: Buffalo Chicken Wings
ing: 2 lb chicken wings, flats and drumettes separated, patted dry
1/2 cup Frank's RedHot Original cayenne pepper sauce
1/2 cup blue cheese dressing, for serving
steps: Adjust oven rack to upper-middle and heat to 450°F. Line a rimmed sheet with foil and set a wire rack on top; brush rack lightly with 1 tbsp frying oil.
In a bowl, toss wings with baking powder, 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp pepper until evenly coated. Arrange skin-side up on rack, spacing slightly.
Bake at 450°F for 35 to 45 minutes, rotating sheet halfway, until skin is deeply browned and crisp and wings reach 165°F internally.
Near the end of baking, melt 4 tbsp butter in a small saucepan over low heat. Whisk in 1/2 cup hot sauce, 1 tsp vinegar, and 1/4 tsp garlic powder; simmer for 1 minute, then remove from heat.
Transfer hot wings to a large bowl. Pour warm sauce over and toss until every piece is coated and glossy.
Rest sauced wings 2 minutes to set, then serve immediately with blue cheese dressing, celery, and carrot sticks.
tip: For extra-crisp skin, air-dry seasoned wings on a rack in the fridge 4 to 12 hours before baking. Prefer frying? Fry at 350°F for 10 to 12 minutes until 175°F, then toss in the same sauce.

title: Southern Fried Chicken
ing: 3 lb bone-in chicken pieces (legs and thighs)
steps: Combine 2 cups buttermilk and 1 tbsp hot sauce in a bowl. Add 3 lb chicken, turn to coat, cover, and refrigerate for 30 minutes (up to 12 hours).
Whisk 2 cups flour, 1/2 cup cornstarch, 2 tsp salt, 1 tsp pepper, 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp onion powder, and 1/2 tsp cayenne in a shallow dish.
Remove chicken from buttermilk, letting excess drip. Dredge in flour mixture, pressing to coat. Set on a rack 10 minutes to set the crust.
Heat frying oil in a Dutch oven to 325°F, at least 2 inches deep. Maintain 315–330°F during frying.
Fry dark meat first: add a few pieces without crowding, skin side down. Fry 14–18 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden brown and 165°F at the thickest part.
Transfer to a rack set over a sheet pan; sprinkle lightly with salt and pepper to taste. Return oil to 325°F between batches.
Fry remaining pieces in batches the same way, 12–16 minutes for smaller pieces, always verifying 165°F internal temperature.
Rest chicken 5 minutes on the rack to keep crisp. Serve hot.
tip: For extra-craggy crust, double-dip: dredge, dip back in buttermilk, dredge again. Keep finished chicken warm on a 250°F rack up to 20 minutes without losing crispness.

title: Nashville Hot Chicken
ing: 2 lb bone-in chicken pieces (legs and thighs)
steps: Pat chicken dry and season lightly with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. In a bowl whisk milk, buttermilk, and hot sauce. Submerge chicken, cover, and chill for 30 minutes while you prep dredge and oil.

In a shallow dish combine flour, cornstarch, 1 1/2 tsp salt, 3/4 tsp pepper, garlic powder, paprika, and cayenne. Remove chicken from marinade, letting excess drip, then dredge thoroughly. Rest coated pieces 10 minutes.
Heat frying oil in a heavy pot to 325°F; oil should be 2 inches deep. Fry chicken in batches, turning occasionally, until deep golden and crisp, 14–18 minutes for thighs, 12–16 minutes for legs.
Verify doneness: insert an instant-read thermometer at the thickest part without touching bone; chicken must reach 165°F. Drain on a rack set over a sheet pan 5 minutes.
While last batch fries, make hot oil paste: in a heatproof bowl whisk lard or neutral oil, cayenne, brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, and salt until smooth.
Ladle or pour 1/2 to 3/4 cup of the fresh frying oil into the spice mixture carefully and whisk until a fluid, brick-red glaze forms. Adjust thickness with more hot oil as needed.
Brush or spoon the hot glaze generously over all sides of the fried chicken. Let set 2 minutes so the crust absorbs the spice oil.
To serve, lay white bread slices on a platter, top with hot chicken, and crown with pickle chips. Serve immediately.
tip: Control heat by adjusting cayenne up or down 1 tbsp. Keep fried chicken warm on a 250°F rack up to 30 minutes before glazing to maintain crispness.

title: Chicken and Waffles
ing: 1 lb chicken thighs, boneless skinless, cut into 8 pieces
1/4 cup maple syrup, plus more for serving
steps: Marinate chicken: In a bowl, whisk 1 cup buttermilk with 1 tsp hot sauce. Add chicken, turn to coat, cover, and refrigerate for 20 minutes while you heat oil and make waffle batter.
Heat oil: Pour frying oil 1 to 1 1/2 inches deep in a heavy skillet or Dutch oven. Heat to 350°F over medium heat; maintain 325–350°F during frying.

Make waffle batter: Whisk 1 3/4 cups milk, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 eggs, and 1/4 cup melted butter. In another bowl whisk 2 cups flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda, and 1/2 tsp salt. Fold dry into wet just until combined.
Cook waffles: Preheat waffle iron. Lightly oil it, then cook batter in batches until golden and crisp, about 4–5 minutes per waffle. Hold finished waffles on a rack in a 200°F oven.

Dredge chicken: Mix 1 1/4 cups flour, 1/4 cup cornstarch, 1 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp paprika, 1/2 tsp pepper, and 1/2 tsp garlic powder. Lift chicken from buttermilk, let excess drip, then coat thoroughly in dredge.
Fry chicken: Fry coated chicken in batches at 325–350°F until deep golden and the thickest piece reaches 165°F, about 5–7 minutes per batch. Drain on a rack; rest 3 minutes.
Serve: Place waffles on plates, top with fried chicken, and drizzle each serving with about 1 tbsp maple syrup. Offer extra warm maple syrup alongside.
tip: Swap thighs for bone-in wings; fry 10–12 min to 165°F. Keep waffles crisp by holding on a wire rack in a 200°F oven up to 30 minutes.

title: Chicken Pot Pie
ing: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut in 1-inch pieces
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Pat chicken dry, season with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high; brown chicken 4–5 minutes, stirring, until no pink on surface. Transfer to a plate.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to skillet; sauté onion, carrot, and celery with remaining 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper until tender, 6–8 minutes. Stir in garlic; cook 30 seconds.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables; cook, stirring, 1 minute. Gradually whisk in chicken broth, then milk. Simmer, stirring, until thick and bubbly, 3–5 minutes.
Stir in browned chicken, peas, parsley, and thyme. Simmer 2 minutes. Taste and adjust salt and pepper to taste. Off heat, let filling cool 5 minutes.
Fit 1 pie dough round into a 9-inch pie dish; spoon in hot filling, mounding slightly. Top with second round; trim excess, fold under, and crimp. Cut 4–5 slits for steam.
Place pie on a rimmed sheet. Bake at 425°F for 25–30 minutes until crust is deep golden and the filling is bubbling. Ensure chicken pieces reach 165°F.
Let rest 10 minutes to set. Slice and serve warm.
tip: Swap thighs with rotisserie chicken (3 cups shredded) and skip browning to save time. Pie keeps 2 days refrigerated; reheat at 350°F until hot and crisp.

title: Chicken and Dumplings
ing: 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: Pat chicken dry and season lightly with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high, add chicken skin-side down, and brown 4 to 5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate; discard all but 1 tbsp fat.
Add onion, carrots, and celery to the pot and cook over medium heat until softened, 5 to 6 minutes. Stir in garlic and cook 30 seconds.

Pour in chicken broth, scraping up browned bits. Return chicken (and juices) to pot, skin removed if desired. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 25 minutes until chicken reaches 175°F and is very tender.

Transfer chicken to a board; when cool enough, discard skin and bones and shred meat. Keep soup at a low simmer. In a small skillet melt 2 tbsp butter over medium heat, whisk in 2 tbsp flour, and cook 1 minute to make a blond roux; whisk roux into the simmering broth to slightly thicken.
Make dumpling dough: In a bowl whisk 1.5 cups flour, baking powder, and 3/4 tsp salt. Cut in 3 tbsp cold butter until crumbly. Stir in milk just until a soft, sticky dough forms; do not overmix.
Return shredded chicken to the pot and taste; season broth with salt and pepper. Maintain a gentle simmer. Using a tablespoon, drop golf-ball-size mounds of dough onto the surface, spacing slightly.
Cover the pot tightly and simmer without lifting the lid for 15 minutes. Dumplings are done when puffed and cooked through (center reaches 200°F or a toothpick comes out clean).
Turn off heat, rest 5 minutes. Ladle into bowls and garnish with chopped parsley. Serve hot.
tip: Swap thighs with a whole cut-up chicken; simmer 10–15 minutes longer to reach tenderness. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; reheat gently with a splash of broth or milk if thick.

title: Chicken à la King
ing: 1 lb chicken breast, cut in 1/2-inch cubes
1/2 cup jarred pimentos, drained and sliced
4 cups cooked egg noodles, hot, for serving
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Pat chicken dry, season with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper, and sear until no longer pink and reaches 165°F, 4–6 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Add 1 tbsp oil and mushrooms to the skillet; cook over medium-high, stirring, until browned and their liquid evaporates, 5–6 minutes. Transfer to the plate with chicken.
Reduce heat to medium. Melt butter in the skillet. Sprinkle in flour and cook, stirring constantly, until pale golden and nutty, 2–3 minutes.
Whisk in sherry; simmer 1 minute. Gradually whisk in chicken broth, then milk; bring to a gentle boil, whisking, and simmer until slightly thickened, 4–5 minutes.
Stir in cream, remaining 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper; simmer 2 minutes. Return chicken and mushrooms with any juices; simmer until heated through and sauce coats a spoon, 2–3 minutes.
Fold in peas, pimentos, and parsley; warm 1–2 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve spooned generously over hot egg noodles.
tip: Swap sherry with dry Madeira or dry vermouth. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; reheat gently, thinning with a splash of broth or milk if needed.

title: Chicken Salad Sandwich
ing: 1 lb cooked chicken breast, finely chopped
1/4 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
1/8 tsp black pepper, or to taste
steps: Combine 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 2 tbsp sour cream, 2 tsp Dijon, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1/4 tsp salt, and 1/8 tsp pepper in a bowl until smooth.
Fold in 1 lb finely chopped cooked chicken, 1 stalk diced celery, 2 tbsp minced red onion, and 1 tbsp chopped parsley until evenly coated.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste; if desired, thin with 1–2 tsp water to reach a creamy but scoopable consistency.
Lay out 8 toasted bread slices; place a lettuce leaf on 4 slices to keep bread crisp.
Mound about 1/2 cup chicken salad on each lettuce-lined slice and spread to edges.
Top with remaining bread slices, press gently, and cut sandwiches in halves or thirds.
Serve immediately, or chill assembled sandwiches for 10 minutes to set before serving.
tip: Use rotisserie chicken for ease; if starting raw, poach breasts to 165°F, cool, then chop. Chicken salad keeps 3 days refrigerated; assemble sandwiches just before serving to prevent soggy bread.

title: Chicken Caesar Salad
ing: 1 cup crusty bread, cut into 1-inch cubes
steps: Heat a skillet over medium; rub chicken with 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp pepper. Cook 5-7 minutes per side to 165°F. Rest 5 minutes, then slice thinly.
Toss bread cubes with 1 tbsp olive oil, 1/4 tsp salt, and minced garlic. Toast on a sheet pan at 375°F for 8-10 minutes, stirring once, until golden. Cool.
In a bowl, whisk grated Parmesan, egg yolk, lemon juice, Dijon, and anchovies until smooth, 30 seconds.
While whisking constantly, stream in 1/2 cup olive oil to form a creamy, emulsified dressing. Season with 1/4 tsp black pepper.
Place chopped romaine in a large bowl. Add enough dressing to coat leaves lightly; toss thoroughly, 30 seconds.
Add warm croutons and sliced chicken; toss again, adding more dressing as needed to lightly cloak everything.
Plate salad. Top with shaved Parmesan and a few extra cracks of black pepper. Serve immediately.
tip: For coddled egg, warm the yolk by setting a whole egg in just-boiled water for 1 minute, then separate. Croutons keep airtight 2 days; recrisp 3 minutes at 350°F.

title: Honey Mustard Chicken Tenders
ing: 1 tbsp parsley, chopped, for garnish, optional
steps: Whisk 1/2 cup Dijon mustard, 1/4 cup honey, 2 tbsp mayonnaise, 1 tbsp vinegar, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp onion powder, 1/2 tsp paprika, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1/4 tsp pepper until smooth; reserve 1/3 cup for dipping.
Pat chicken dry. Season with remaining 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. Set up breading: bowl of 1/2 cup flour, bowl of 2 beaten eggs, and bowl of 1 cup panko.
Dredge each tender in flour, shake excess; dip in egg; press into panko to coat all sides. Place on a rack and rest 5 minutes to set coating.
Heat 1/4 inch frying oil in a large skillet over medium to medium-high to 350°F. Fry tenders in batches 3–4 minutes per side until deep golden.
Check doneness: chicken must reach 165°F at the thickest point. Transfer to a rack and keep warm while finishing remaining batches, adding oil as needed.
Toss hot tenders lightly with the remaining honey-mustard (not the reserved dipping sauce) or drizzle over just before serving.
Serve immediately with reserved dipping sauce and sprinkle with chopped parsley. Optional: warm sauce in a pan over low heat for 1–2 minutes before serving.
tip: Swap: use 1/2 cup crushed cornflakes mixed with 1/2 cup panko for extra crunch. To bake: place on a greased rack, spray, bake at 425°F for 14–16 min, flipping once, to 165°F.

title: Homemade Chicken Nuggets
ing: 1 1/2 lb chicken breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
steps: In a bowl, combine chicken pieces, buttermilk, 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp pepper; stir to coat, cover, and chill for 20 minutes while you prepare the dredge.
In a shallow dish, whisk flour, cornstarch, garlic powder, paprika, and baking powder. In a second dish, whisk eggs with water to loosen.
Drain excess buttermilk from chicken. Working in batches, dip chicken in flour mix, then egg, then back in flour, pressing to form a craggy coating; place on a rack for 5 minutes.
Pour frying oil into a heavy pot to 1 1/2 inches depth. Heat over medium to 350°F, monitoring with a thermometer.
Fry half the nuggets at 350°F until deep golden and the thickest piece reaches 165°F, about 4 to 6 minutes; adjust heat to maintain 325–350°F.
Transfer nuggets to a rack set over a sheet pan; season lightly with salt and pepper while hot. Repeat frying with remaining nuggets.
Return all nuggets to the oil for a 30–45 second hot flash at 350°F for extra crispness, then drain again on the rack.
Rest 3 minutes before serving to allow juices to settle; serve hot with preferred dipping sauces.
tip: Swap buttermilk with 1 cup milk plus 1 tbsp lemon juice; rest 10 minutes. Leftovers keep 2 days refrigerated; re-crisp on a rack at 400°F for 8–10 minutes.

title: Popcorn Chicken
ing: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, 3/4-inch pieces
1 tbsp chopped parsley, for garnish, optional
steps: Whisk 1 cup buttermilk with 1 tsp hot sauce in a bowl. Add 1 lb chicken pieces, toss to coat, cover, and chill for 20 minutes while you prepare dredging.
In a shallow dish, mix 1 1/2 cups flour, 1/2 cup cornstarch, 2 tsp salt, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper, and cayenne.
In another bowl, beat 2 eggs with 2 tbsp water. Remove chicken from buttermilk, letting excess drip. Dip in egg, then dredge in flour mixture, pressing to adhere. Set on a rack 5 minutes.
Heat frying oil to 350°F in a deep pot (oil depth about 2 inches). Maintain 325–350°F for even browning.
Fry chicken in batches 2–3 minutes, turn, then 2–3 minutes more until deep golden and 165°F internal. Do not crowd; drain on a rack set over a sheet pan.
Return fried pieces for a 30–45 second hot oil refry at 350°F for extra crispness; drain again. Season lightly with 1 tsp kosher salt to taste while hot.
Rest 3 minutes to allow juices to settle. Garnish with chopped parsley if using and serve immediately with your favorite dipping sauce.
tip: Swap thighs with breast if preferred; cut to equal size for even frying. Keep batches hot and crisp in a 250°F oven up to 20 minutes. Leftovers re-crisp in a 400°F oven for 8–10 minutes.

title: Beer Can Chicken
steps: Preheat grill to 375°F for indirect heat (two-zone fire). Clean and oil grates. If using an oven, set to 375°F and place a rack over a rimmed sheet.
Pat chicken dry. Rub outside and cavity with olive oil. Mix salt, pepper, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, thyme, and brown sugar; season chicken all over and inside cavity.
Open beer can and pour out (or drink) about 1/4 cup. Using a knife, poke 2 extra holes near the top rim. Squeeze lemon halves lightly into the can, then drop one lemon half into the can.
Sit the chicken upright over the beer can so the can fits into the cavity and the legs form a stable tripod with the can. Tuck wing tips behind the back.

Place upright chicken on the cool side of the grill (or prepared sheet in oven). Close lid and roast at 375°F for 60 to 75 minutes, rotating once, until thickest breast reaches 160°F and thigh reaches 175°F.
If skin needs more color, move briefly over direct heat or increase oven to 425°F for 5 to 8 minutes, watching closely to avoid burning.
Carefully remove chicken from heat. Using tongs and a spatula, lift chicken off the can—avoid hot steam—then rest on a board for 10 minutes.
Carve into breasts, thighs, drumsticks, and wings. Serve with pan juices and a squeeze of the remaining lemon half.
tip: Use a sturdy half-full can and a flat surface for stability. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; reheat covered at 300°F until warm. Try lager or pale ale; avoid very sweet or heavily hopped beers.

title: Lemon Herb Roast Chicken
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Set a rack in the lower third. Tuck wings under the chicken and tie legs with kitchen twine for even roasting.
In a small bowl mix olive oil, salt, pepper, lemon zest, thyme, rosemary, parsley, and oregano to form a paste. Rub all over chicken, including under the breast skin.
Stuff cavity with the lemon halves and smashed garlic. Place chicken breast-side up in a roasting pan. Scatter potatoes and carrots around; pour chicken broth into the pan.
Roast at 425°F for 20 minutes to brown the skin, then reduce oven to 375°F and continue roasting for 35–45 minutes, basting once, until juices run clear.
Check doneness: insert an instant-read thermometer into the thickest part of the thigh without touching bone; it must read 165°F.
Transfer chicken to a board and tent loosely with foil. Let rest for 10–15 minutes so juices redistribute.
Toss vegetables in pan juices and return to oven at 375°F for 5 minutes if needed to glaze. Skim excess fat from pan juices for serving.
Carve chicken: remove legs, thighs, and wings; slice breasts across the grain. Serve with roasted vegetables and spooned pan juices.
tip: Swap baby potatoes for thick-cut onions or parsnips. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; reheat covered at 325°F with a splash of broth to keep moist.

title: Chicken Parmesan
steps: Pound cutlets to 1/2-inch thickness if needed. Pat dry, then season both sides with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper.
Set up dredge: bowl 1 flour; bowl 2 eggs beaten with 1 tbsp water; bowl 3 breadcrumbs mixed with Parmesan, garlic powder, and oregano.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shake excess; dip in egg; coat in breadcrumb-Parmesan mix, pressing to adhere. Rest breaded cutlets 5 minutes.
Heat 1/4 inch vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high until shimmering, about 375°F. Fry cutlets in batches until golden, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Drain on rack.
Warm marinara in a saucepan over medium heat until simmering, 3 to 5 minutes; keep hot.
Heat oven to 425°F. Spoon a thin layer of marinara in a 9x13-inch baking dish. Nestle cutlets, top each with sauce, then mozzarella slices. Drizzle with 1 tbsp olive oil.
Bake at 425°F until cheese is melted, bubbling, and chicken reaches 165°F in the thickest part, 10 to 12 minutes. Broil 1 to 2 minutes for added browning if desired.
Rest 5 minutes. Scatter basil over top and serve immediately with extra warm sauce on the side.
tip: Use plain breadcrumbs plus 1 tsp Italian seasoning if needed. Fry cutlets ahead and refrigerate 1 day; sauce and bake just before serving to keep the crust crisp.

title: Chicken Tortilla Soup
ing: 4 oz corn tortillas, cut into thin strips
1 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
1/2 tsp black pepper, or to taste
steps: Warm 2 tbsp oil in a pot over medium and pan-fry tortilla strips in batches until crisp and lightly golden, 3–4 minutes; drain on paper towels and set aside.
In the same pot, char tomatoes, onion, and garlic over medium-high, turning until lightly blistered, 6–8 minutes. Blend with chipotle and 1 cup broth until smooth.
Return puree to the pot with remaining 3 cups broth. Nestle in chicken thighs, bring to a boil, then lower to a steady simmer for 25–30 minutes until chicken reaches 165°F.
Transfer chicken to a plate; cool slightly, then remove skin and bones and shred meat. Skim excess fat from soup if desired.
Return shredded chicken to the pot. Season with salt, pepper, and lime juice; simmer 5 minutes to marry flavors.
To serve, divide crispy tortilla strips among bowls. Ladle hot soup over to soften some strips while keeping others crisp.
Garnish each bowl with queso fresco, crema, avocado, and cilantro. Serve immediately with extra lime wedges if desired.
tip: For a milder heat, swap the chipotle for 1 small pasilla or guajillo soaked and blended. Tortilla strips stay crisp if stored airtight; add to bowls just before serving.

title: Chicken Jambalaya
ing: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut in 1-inch cubes
8 oz andouille sausage, halved lengthwise and sliced
1 1/2 cups long-grain white rice, rinsed and drained
3/4 cup green bell pepper, finely chopped
2 tbsp green onions, thinly sliced, for garnish
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a heavy 4- to 5-qt pot over medium-high until shimmering. Brown sausage 4 minutes; transfer to a plate. Add 1 tsp more oil if needed, then brown chicken 5 to 6 minutes until lightly colored.

Reduce heat to medium. Add onion, bell pepper, and celery; cook 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until softened and golden at edges. Stir in garlic, paprika, thyme, salt, black pepper, and cayenne; cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in rice to coat with aromatics; cook 1 minute. Return sausage and any juices. Add drained tomatoes and chicken broth; scrape up browned bits to deglaze.
Bring to a boil over medium-high, then cover, reduce to low, and simmer for 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
After 20 minutes, quickly uncover, gently fluff from bottom, re-cover, and continue to simmer on low for 5 to 10 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat and let stand covered for 5 minutes to finish steaming. Taste and adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Fluff again, fold in half the green onions, and serve hot, garnished with remaining green onions.
tip: Use long-grain rice like Louisiana-grown. For a drier, browner jambalaya, omit tomatoes and add 1/4 cup extra broth. Leftovers keep 3 days chilled; reheat covered with a splash of broth.

title: Chicken and Sausage Gumbo
ing: 1 lb chicken thighs, boneless skinless, cut into 1-inch pieces
8 oz andouille sausage, halved lengthwise and sliced 1/4-inch thick
1 cup green bell pepper, finely chopped
1 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
1/2 tsp black pepper, or to taste
2 tbsp scallions, thinly sliced, for garnish
2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
2 cups cooked white rice, warm, for serving
steps: Brown sausage in a large heavy pot over medium heat until well browned, 5 to 7 minutes; transfer to a plate, leaving drippings. Season chicken lightly with salt and pepper, brown in drippings 6 to 8 minutes; transfer.
Make a dark roux: add vegetable oil and flour to the pot. Cook over medium-low, stirring constantly with a flat wooden spoon, until chocolate-brown, 25 to 35 minutes. Do not let it burn.
Stir in onion, bell pepper, and celery; cook until softened and fragrant, 6 to 8 minutes. Add garlic and cook 30 seconds until aromatic.
Whisk in chicken stock gradually until smooth. Add thyme, bay leaf, cayenne, browned sausage, and chicken with any juices. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer.
Simmer uncovered, skimming fat, until chicken is tender and flavors meld, 45 to 60 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Taste and adjust salt, black pepper, and cayenne. Remove bay leaf. If desired, skim more fat. Gumbo should be slightly thick; simmer longer to reduce or add a splash of stock to loosen.
Serve gumbo hot over warm cooked white rice. Garnish with scallions and parsley. Ensure chicken pieces reach 165°F internal temperature before serving.
tip: For deeper flavor, substitute 1 cup stock with seafood stock. Gumbo tastes better next day; cool quickly and refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat gently, thinning with stock if too thick.

title: Huli Huli Chicken
ing: 1 tbsp neutral frying oil, as needed
1 tbsp green onions, thinly sliced, for garnish, as needed
steps: Whisk ketchup, pineapple juice, soy sauce, brown sugar, rice vinegar, ginger, garlic, and sesame oil in a bowl until dissolved and smooth.
Set aside 1/2 cup sauce for basting. Place chicken and remaining sauce in a zip bag; expel air, seal, and marinate refrigerated for at least 1 hour and up to 12 hours.
Remove chicken, pat dry, and discard used marinade. Oil grill grates with neutral oil. Heat grill to medium (about 375°F).
Grill chicken skin side down over direct heat 5 to 6 minutes until well marked; flip and grill 5 minutes more.
Move to indirect heat, cover, and cook 15 minutes. Begin huli (turning) and baste with reserved sauce every 3 to 4 minutes for 15 to 20 minutes more.
Continue turning and basting until glazed and the thickest part reads 175°F for thighs, total 35 to 45 minutes grilling.
Transfer to a platter, tent loosely with foil, and rest 5 minutes to let juices settle.
Slice or serve whole, spoon any juices over, and garnish with green onions.
tip: For oven: roast at 400°F on a rack 35 to 40 min, broil 2 to 3 min to char, basting with reserved sauce. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; rewarm gently to preserve glaze.

title: Chicken Fajitas
ing: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, sliced 1/2-inch thick
2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish
1 lime, cut into wedges, for serving
1 tbsp vegetable oil, as needed for frying
steps: In a bowl, combine lime juice, 2 tbsp vegetable oil, salt, cumin, chili powder, smoked paprika, garlic powder, and black pepper. Add chicken and toss to coat; marinate for 10 minutes.
Heat a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high until just smoking, about 3 minutes. Add 1 tbsp oil as needed, then spread chicken in an even layer.
Sear without stirring for 2 minutes, then cook, stirring occasionally, until browned and cooked through to 165°F, 5 to 6 minutes total. Transfer chicken to a warm plate.
Add onion and bell peppers to the skillet with a pinch of salt. Cook over medium-high, stirring, until tender-crisp and lightly charred, 5 to 6 minutes.
Return chicken and any juices to the skillet. Toss with vegetables over medium heat until glossy and hot, about 1 minute. Adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Warm tortillas in a dry skillet over medium heat for 30 seconds per side or wrap in foil and heat at 300°F for 5 minutes.
Serve chicken and peppers sizzling-hot with warm tortillas, cilantro, and lime wedges. Let diners fill tortillas at the table.
tip: Swap thighs for 1 1/2 lb sliced chicken breast if preferred. Keep leftovers up to 3 days refrigerated; reheat in a hot skillet to revive the sear. Add jalapeño with peppers for heat.

title: Chicken Enchiladas
ing: 2 oz serrano or jalapeño chiles, stemmed
1/2 cup cilantro leaves and stems, loosely packed
4 oz Oaxaca or Monterey Jack cheese, shredded
1/4 cup white onion, finely diced, for garnish
steps: Simmer chicken in 4 cups broth with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper over medium heat until tender and 165°F in the thickest part, about 18–22 minutes. Transfer to a plate; reserve 1 cup cooking broth.
Shred chicken with two forks. Moisten with 2–3 tbsp reserved broth so it stays juicy; set aside.
Make salsa verde: Boil tomatillos, chiles, onion, and garlic in water to cover until tomatillos turn olive-green, 7–8 minutes. Drain well.
Blend boiled veg with cilantro, 1 tsp salt, cumin, and 1/2 cup reserved chicken broth until smooth. Adjust thickness with more broth if needed.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium. Pour in salsa and simmer, stirring, until it deepens and slightly thickens, 6–8 minutes. Season to taste; keep warm on low.

Warm 12 corn tortillas until pliable (skillet or 300°F oven, 5 minutes). Lightly oil a skillet with 1 tbsp oil over medium and quickly pass each tortilla in the hot oil 5–7 seconds per side to prevent tearing.
Dip a tortilla in warm salsa, place 2–3 tbsp shredded chicken down the center, sprinkle a little cheese, roll into a cylinder, and set seam-side down on a warm plate. Repeat with remaining tortillas.
Spoon more salsa over enchiladas, top with remaining cheese and let melt 1–2 minutes. Finish with crema, diced onion, cilantro, and lime wedges; serve immediately.
tip: Swap: use rotisserie chicken to save time. Keep tortillas warm wrapped in a towel. Leftovers keep 2 days refrigerated; reheat gently with extra salsa to prevent drying.

title: Chicken Quesadillas
ing: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, finely chopped
steps: Season chicken with salt, pepper, cumin, and oregano; toss well. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium-high until shimmering, then add chicken and cook, stirring, until browned and cooked to 165°F, 6 to 8 minutes.

Reduce heat to medium. Add onion and cook until translucent, 3 minutes. Stir in garlic and cook 30 seconds. Fold in tomatoes and cilantro; cook until most moisture evaporates, 2 to 3 minutes. Transfer to a bowl.
Wipe skillet and heat over medium. Warm tortillas 30 seconds per side to make pliable. Keep covered with a towel.
Assemble each quesadilla: spread 2 tbsp mixed cheeses on half of a tortilla, add 1/4 cup chicken mixture, top with 2 more tbsp cheese, and fold to close.
Add a thin film of oil to skillet over medium. Cook folded quesadillas in batches until tortillas are spotty golden and cheese melts, 2 to 3 minutes per side. Adjust heat to prevent scorching.
Hold finished quesadillas on a rack or sheet at 200°F while cooking remaining batches to keep crisp.
Slice each quesadilla into wedges and serve hot with lime wedges. Salt to taste if needed.
tip: Swap Oaxaca/Chihuahua with low-moisture mozzarella and mild Monterey Jack if unavailable. Keep leftovers wrapped and chilled up to 2 days; re-crisp on a dry skillet over medium heat.

title: Chicken Tinga Tacos
ing: 3 oz canned chipotle chiles in adobo, with sauce
4 oz queso fresco, crumbled, for garnish
1/2 cup fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish
1 lime, cut into wedges, for serving
steps: Place chicken in a pot with 1/2 cup broth and a pinch of salt; bring to a gentle boil, then cover and simmer over low heat for 12–15 minutes until chicken reaches 165°F. Rest 5 minutes, then shred.
While chicken cooks, char tomatoes, onion slices, and garlic in a dry skillet over medium-high, turning until blistered (6–8 minutes). Peel any very blackened tomato skins if desired.
Blend charred tomatoes, onion, garlic, chipotles with adobo, remaining 1/2 cup broth, oregano, cumin, 1 tsp salt, and pepper until smooth.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide skillet over medium. Pour in the sauce; simmer for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until slightly thick and glossy.
Stir in shredded chicken; simmer 3–4 minutes to coat and heat through. Adjust salt and chipotle to taste; the tinga should be saucy, not dry.
Warm corn tortillas on a dry skillet over medium for 30–45 seconds per side until pliable.
Assemble tacos: spoon tinga into tortillas and top with queso fresco and cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.
Optional: keep tinga warm over low heat, adding a splash of broth if it thickens. Keep tortillas wrapped in a towel.
tip: Swap: use all thighs for richer tinga. Make-ahead: Tinga keeps 3 days refrigerated; rewarm with a splash of broth. Traditional toppings: onion, cilantro, queso fresco—avoid overloading to keep tortillas intact.

title: Chicken Mole Poblano
ing: 2 lb bone-in chicken thighs, skin removed
2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried pasilla chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
1 slice bolillo bread (or 1 oz French bread), torn
1 tbsp lard or frying oil, as needed
steps: Place chicken and 3 cups broth in a pot; add 1/2 tsp salt. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, cover, and cook until tender and 175°F at bone, about 35–40 minutes. Reserve meat and broth separately.

Toast ancho, pasilla, and mulato chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat until pliable and fragrant, 30–45 seconds per side. Soak in hot water for 15 minutes; drain, reserving 1/2 cup soaking liquid.

In the same skillet, add 1–2 tbsp lard or oil. Fry tortilla and bread until golden, 2–3 minutes; remove. Fry plantain slices until browned, 3–4 minutes; remove. Lightly fry onion and garlic until softened, 4–5 minutes; remove.
Toast sesame seeds, pumpkin seeds, almonds, peanuts, and clove in the dry skillet over medium-low heat, 2–3 minutes, stirring; do not burn. Add raisins for last 30 seconds to plump.

Blend soaked chiles with tomato, fried onion and garlic, fried bread and tortilla, plantain, nuts and seeds, raisins, cinnamon, chocolate, 1 cup reserved broth, and 1/2 cup chile soaking liquid until very smooth, 1–2 minutes, adding broth as needed.
Heat 1 tbsp lard or oil in a wide pot over medium. Carefully pour in the puree; simmer and stir as it sputters until thickened, 10–12 minutes. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Stir in 1–1 1/2 cups reserved broth to reach a nappé sauce. Add chicken pieces, coat in mole, and simmer on low for 10–15 minutes to meld flavors, keeping at a gentle bubble.
Serve chicken ladled with mole and extra sauce. Sprinkle with a pinch of toasted sesame seeds if desired and accompany with warm tortillas and rice.
tip: Mulato can be subbed with more ancho if unavailable. Mole improves overnight; chill up to 3 days or freeze 2 months. Thin with warm broth when reheating.

title: Chicken Pozole
ing: 1 cup packed cilantro, tender stems and leaves
2 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
1 tsp black pepper, or to taste
2 (25 oz) cans white hominy, rinsed and drained
1/2 cup radishes, thinly sliced, for garnish
1/2 cup white onion, finely diced, for garnish
steps: Season 1.5 lb chicken thighs with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pot over medium-high and brown chicken 4–5 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, add 8 cups chicken stock and return chicken to the pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer for 25 minutes, skimming foam. Cook to 175°F at the thickest part.
Meanwhile, broil tomatillos, jalapeños, and poblano on a sheet 4–6 inches from heat, turning until blistered, 6–8 minutes. Cool, then peel poblano if desired.
Blend broiled tomatillos, jalapeños, poblano, 1 cup onion, 4 cloves garlic, 1 cup cilantro, 1 tbsp oregano, and 2 tsp cumin until very smooth, 45–60 seconds.

Remove chicken to a plate. Strain and reserve broth if needed. Shred meat, discarding skin and bones. Return pot to medium heat, add a little oil, and fry the green sauce, stirring, until thickened and darker, 5–7 minutes.
Pour reserved broth into the fried sauce and bring to a simmer. Stir in hominy and shredded chicken. Simmer gently for 15–20 minutes; adjust salt and pepper to taste. Add lime juice to brighten.
Warm bowls. Ladle pozole and let stand 2 minutes to settle flavors. Serve hot with shredded cabbage, radishes, diced onion, chopped cilantro, and lime wedges for squeezing.
tip: For milder heat, seed the jalapeños before broiling. Pozole improves overnight; chill up to 3 days. Skim fat after chilling for a cleaner broth.

title: Chicken Chilaquiles
ing: 12 oz corn tortillas, cut into wedges
steps: Poach chicken: Bring 4 cups chicken broth to a gentle simmer over medium heat, add 1/2 tsp salt if broth is unsalted, slide in 1 lb chicken breasts, and simmer for 12–15 minutes until 165°F. Transfer to a plate to cool.

Make salsa verde: Simmer tomatillos, jalapeños, onion, and garlic in the poaching broth for 6–8 minutes until tomatillos pale and soften. Scoop solids to a blender with 1/2 cup cilantro and 1 tsp kosher salt; blend smooth.
Reduce salsa: Pour blended salsa into a skillet and simmer over medium heat for 5–7 minutes until slightly thickened and bright. Adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Shred chicken: Shred the cooled chicken into bite-size pieces and keep warm; moisten with a few spoonfuls of salsa to prevent drying.
Fry tortillas: Heat 1/2 inch frying oil in a wide skillet to 350°F. Fry tortilla wedges in batches for 2–3 minutes until crisp and lightly golden. Drain on paper towels and lightly salt.
Coat chips: Bring salsa to a lively simmer, add half the chips, toss gently to coat, then add remaining chips and shredded chicken. Cook 1–2 minutes, just until chips soften at edges but stay sturdy.
Finish and serve: Divide onto 4 plates. Top with Mexican crema, queso fresco, thin onion, avocado, and chopped cilantro. Serve immediately with lime wedges.
tip: For milder heat, seed the jalapeños. To save time, use a rotisserie chicken. Chips can be fried a few hours ahead; keep uncovered to stay crisp.

title: Arroz con Pollo
ing: 1/2 cup green bell pepper, finely diced
1 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish
steps: Pat chicken dry, season with 1 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wide pot over medium-high until shimmering, then brown chicken skin-side down 6–8 minutes; flip and brown 3–4 minutes. Transfer out.

Lower heat to medium. In the same pot, sauté onion and green bell pepper for 4–5 minutes until softened, stirring to lift browned bits. Add garlic, cumin, paprika, and oregano; cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in rinsed rice and toast 1–2 minutes, coating grains in oil and aromatics. Add crushed tomatoes and broth; bring to a brisk simmer over medium-high heat.
Nestle chicken, skin-side up, into the rice. Reduce to low, cover, and simmer gently for 25–30 minutes until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Maintain a gentle bubble; do not stir.
Check chicken for doneness: thighs should reach 175°F at the thickest part and juices run clear. If needed, cook covered 5 more minutes.
Remove pot from heat. Sprinkle in peas and pimientos, cover, and let stand 5–10 minutes off heat to steam and warm through.
Fluff rice gently with a fork without breaking grains. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste, and rest 2 minutes.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve hot, ensuring each plate gets chicken, rice, peas, and pimientos.
tip: Swap: use 1/4 tsp turmeric or a pinch of saffron for color. Make-ahead: cool, refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat covered with a splash of broth over low heat until hot.

title: Peruvian Roast Chicken (Pollo a la Brasa)
ing: 1 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish
steps: Pat the chicken very dry and tuck wing tips. In a bowl mix salt, pepper, cumin, paprika, oregano, garlic, soy sauce, lime juice, vinegar, 2 tbsp oil, and sugar into a paste.
Rub marinade under the skin over breasts and all over the chicken. Marinate 30–60 minutes at room temp or up to 24 hours refrigerated; if chilled, bring to room temp 30 minutes before roasting.
Heat oven to 425°F. Toss potatoes with 1 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt and pepper. Place in a roasting pan with a rack or arrange around where the chicken will sit.
Set chicken breast-side up on rack or atop potato bed. Roast at 425°F for 50–60 minutes, rotating pan once, until thighs reach 165°F and juices run clear.
Rest chicken 10–15 minutes. If potatoes need more color, return them to oven at 425°F for 5–10 minutes while the chicken rests.
Carve the chicken into legs, thighs, wings, and sliced breast. Toss potatoes with any pan juices.
Serve chicken and potatoes hot, spooning juices over. Garnish with chopped cilantro and pass lime wedges if desired.
tip: For extra authenticity, add 1 tsp ají panca paste to the marinade. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; reheat at 350°F until warm. Serve with ají verde and a simple salad.

title: Aji de Gallina
ing: 4 slices white sandwich bread, crusts removed
1/4 tsp black pepper, or to taste
8 olives, Peruvian black or Kalamata, pitted, for serving
2 cups cooked white rice, for serving
steps: Poach chicken: Add 1 lb chicken breasts and 4 cups chicken broth to a pot, bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook until the thickest part reaches 165°F, about 12–15 minutes. Transfer chicken to a plate; reserve 2 cups broth.
Shred chicken: When cool enough to handle, shred chicken into bite-size strands. Strain and keep the reserved poaching broth warm.

Make flavor base: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a saucepan over medium. Add onion and cook until translucent, 8–10 minutes. Stir in garlic, cumin, and turmeric; cook 1 minute. Add aji amarillo paste; cook, stirring, 2 minutes.
Blend bread sauce: Tear 4 bread slices into a blender. Add 1 cup evaporated milk and 1 cup reserved warm broth; blend until perfectly smooth, 30–45 seconds.

Build the stew: Stir the bread-milk puree into the onion-aji base. Add walnuts and Parmesan; cook over low, stirring, until thick and silky, 5–7 minutes. Loosen with more warm broth as needed for a creamy spoonable sauce.

Finish with chicken: Fold in shredded chicken; simmer gently on low, stirring, 3–5 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Sauce should be lush, not stiff; adjust with broth to reach a thick creaminess.
Serve: Mound cooked white rice on plates. Spoon Aji de Gallina alongside. Garnish with parsley, arrange hard-boiled egg quarters and olives on top. Serve hot.
tip: If using dried aji amarillo pods, seed/soak and blend with a little broth to make paste. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; reheat gently with a splash of broth or milk to restore creaminess.

title: Chicken Cacciatore
ing: 2 lb bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks
2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: Pat chicken dry, season with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a wide heavy skillet over medium-high until shimmering, then brown chicken 4 to 5 minutes per side; transfer to a plate.

Lower heat to medium. Add onion and bell pepper; cook, stirring, until softened, 6 to 8 minutes. Add mushrooms and cook until they release liquid and begin to brown, 5 to 6 minutes. Stir in sliced garlic for 30 seconds.
Deglaze with 1/2 cup white wine, scraping browned bits; simmer 2 minutes until mostly reduced.
Stir in 1 cup crushed tomatoes, 1/2 cup chicken broth, capers, rosemary, and thyme. Return chicken skin-side up, nestling in sauce; bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Cover and simmer gently for 25 minutes, then uncover and continue to simmer until chicken is tender and reaches 165°F at the thickest part, 10 to 15 minutes more.
Discard herb sprigs. Stir in olives and 1 tbsp red wine vinegar; simmer 2 minutes. Adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Rest off heat 5 minutes to settle flavors. Sprinkle with 2 tbsp chopped parsley and serve with polenta or crusty bread.
tip: For a Tuscan-style version, omit peppers and mushrooms, add 1 chopped carrot and 1 chopped celery stalk with the onion. Cacciatore improves overnight; chill up to 3 days and rewarm gently.

title: Chicken Marsala
ing: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, pounded 1/2-inch thick
steps: Pat cutlets dry; season both sides with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Dredge lightly in 1/2 cup flour, shaking off excess.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil and 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Sear chicken in a single layer, 3 to 4 minutes per side, to 165°F. Transfer to a warm plate.
Add 1 tbsp olive oil to the skillet. Sauté sliced mushrooms over medium-high, stirring, until browned and their liquid evaporates, 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic; cook 30 seconds until fragrant, scraping browned bits from the pan with a wooden spoon.
Pour in 3/4 cup dry Marsala; boil, scraping up fond, until reduced by about half, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add 3/4 cup chicken broth; simmer for 5 to 6 minutes until slightly syrupy and coats a spoon. Stir in 1 tsp lemon juice.
Return chicken and any juices to the pan; simmer, turning once, until warmed through and glazed, 2 minutes. Off heat, whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter to silkiness.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley and adjust seasoning to taste. Serve immediately with the pan sauce spooned over.
tip: Use true dry Marsala (not sweet). Keep cutlets thin for quick, even cooking. Leftovers keep 2 days refrigerated; rewarm gently to avoid breaking the sauce.

title: Chicken Piccata
ing: 2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: Pound chicken cutlets to 1/4-inch thickness between plastic. Pat dry. Season both sides with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper.
Dredge cutlets lightly in flour, shaking off excess. Heat 2 tbsp oil and 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high until shimmering, about 2 minutes.
Sear cutlets in batches without crowding until golden, 2 to 3 minutes per side, reaching 165°F internal. Transfer to a warm plate; tent loosely with foil. Add more oil if needed.
Pour off excess fat, leaving browned bits. Add wine; simmer over medium-high, scraping fond, until reduced by half, about 2 minutes.
Stir in chicken broth, lemon juice, and zest; simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until lightly syrupy.
Reduce heat to low. Add capers, then whisk in 2 tbsp cold butter, one piece at a time, to emulsify, 30 to 60 seconds. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste.
Return cutlets and any juices to the pan; turn to coat and warm through for 1 minute over low heat.
Transfer to a platter. Spoon sauce over, garnish with parsley and lemon slices, and serve immediately.
tip: Use thin chicken breasts or slice whole breasts horizontally. Sauce can be made 1 day ahead; rewarm gently and finish with the final butter just before serving.

title: Chicken Saltimbocca
ing: 1 tbsp fresh parsley, finely chopped, for garnish
steps: Pat chicken dry, season both sides with 1/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper, then lightly dredge in 1/2 cup flour, shaking off excess.
Lay 2 sage leaves on each cutlet and top with 2 slices prosciutto, pressing so prosciutto adheres; if needed, secure with toothpicks.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil and 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high until foaming, 1 minute. Add cutlets prosciutto-side down; cook 2 to 3 minutes until lightly crisp.
Flip and cook 2 to 3 minutes more until chicken is just cooked through to 165°F. Transfer to a warm plate; tent loosely with foil.
Pour off excess fat, then add remaining 1 tbsp olive oil to the skillet. Deglaze with 1/2 cup white wine over medium heat, scraping browned bits, and reduce by half, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Add 1/2 cup broth and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until slightly syrupy. Stir in remaining 1 tbsp butter and 1 tbsp lemon juice off heat; swirl until glossy.
Return cutlets to the pan, spoon sauce over, and warm 30 to 60 seconds. Discard toothpicks. Adjust seasoning to taste.
Transfer to plates, spoon pan sauce over, and garnish with parsley. Serve immediately.
tip: Use Marsala instead of white wine for a richer sauce. Keep cooked cutlets warm in a 200°F oven while finishing the sauce; leftovers keep 2 days refrigerated and reheat gently in the sauce.

title: Chicken Milanese
ing: 1/4 cup olive oil, for frying, as needed
1 cup baby arugula, for garnish, as needed
steps: Lay chicken between plastic; pound to 1/4 inch. Pat dry and season both sides with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper.
Set up dredging: shallow dish with flour; second with eggs beaten with milk and a pinch of salt; third with breadcrumbs mixed with Parmigiano, remaining salt, and pepper.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking excess; dip in egg; press into breadcrumb mixture until thoroughly coated. Rest coated cutlets 5 minutes.
Heat 1/4 inch olive oil in a large skillet over medium to medium-high until shimmering, about 350°F.
Fry cutlets in batches without crowding, 2 to 3 minutes per side, until deep golden and cooked through to 165°F internal. Adjust heat to maintain gentle sizzle.
Drain on a rack or paper towels; lightly season with a pinch of salt while hot.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges; top each cutlet with a small handful of arugula and a drizzle of pan oil or fresh olive oil.
tip: Use fine dry breadcrumbs for the most classic texture; avoid panko. Keep cutlets thin and oil fresh for crisp results. Leftovers re-crisp in a 400°F oven for 6–8 minutes.

title: Chicken Cordon Bleu
steps: Arrange cutlets between plastic and pound to 1/4-inch. Pat dry, then season both sides with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper.
Lay 1 slice ham and 1 slice Swiss on each cutlet, leaving a 1/2-inch border. Tightly roll from the short end and secure with toothpicks; chill 10 minutes.
Prepare breading: place 1/2 cup flour in one dish. Beat 2 eggs with 1 tbsp water in a second. Mix breadcrumbs, Parmesan, and thyme in a third.
Dredge rolls in flour, dip in egg, then coat evenly in breadcrumb mixture. Rest 5 minutes to set the crust.
Heat frying oil in a large skillet over medium heat to 350°F. Sear rolls, turning, until golden on all sides, 4 to 5 minutes total.
Transfer to a rack on a sheet pan and bake at 375°F until the thickest part reaches 165°F, about 15 to 18 minutes. Tent and rest 5 minutes; remove toothpicks.
Make sauce: melt 2 tbsp butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in 1 tbsp flour; cook 1 minute. Slowly whisk in broth, then cream; simmer for 3 to 4 minutes.
Whisk in Dijon and lemon juice; season with pepper to taste. Spoon sauce over chicken and garnish with parsley before serving.
tip: Chill rolled cutlets briefly to help them hold shape while breading. For advance prep, bread up to 8 hours ahead and refrigerate; pan-sear and bake just before serving.

title: Chicken Kiev
ing: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, 6-7 oz each
steps: Mash 8 tbsp butter with parsley, dill, lemon zest, and garlic until smooth. Shape into a 4x1-inch log, wrap, and freeze until very firm, about 20 minutes.
Trim chicken breasts. With a sharp knife, create a deep pocket from the thick side without piercing through. Season inside and out with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper.
Cut the butter log into 4 equal batons. Insert one baton deep into each pocket. Press to seal, then tightly roll the breast around the butter, tucking sides in to enclose.
Set up breading: place 1/2 cup flour, 2 beaten eggs, and 1 cup breadcrumbs in separate shallow dishes. Dredge each roll in flour, dip in egg, then coat in breadcrumbs, pressing to adhere.
Repeat a second egg-and-breadcrumb pass for a thick seal. Chill the breaded rolls seam-side down until firm, 20 minutes, to help prevent leaking.
Heat 1/2 cup frying oil in a skillet over medium to 350°F. Shallow-fry rolls, turning, until golden on all sides, 4-6 minutes total. Transfer to a rack on a sheet pan.
Bake at 400°F until an instant-read thermometer in the thick center reads 165°F and butter just begins to sizzle, 12-15 minutes. Rest 5 minutes to set juices.
Serve immediately, slicing to reveal the herbed butter. Season with additional salt and pepper to taste if needed.
tip: Chill or briefly freeze after breading to reduce butter leaks. Leftovers keep 2 days refrigerated; reheat at 325°F until hot to maintain crust.

title: Chicken Schnitzel
steps: Pound chicken cutlets between plastic wrap to 1/4-inch thickness using a mallet; pat dry.
Set up breading: place flour in one shallow dish; beat eggs with milk, salt, and pepper in a second; place breadcrumbs in a third.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, shaking off excess; dip in egg, letting excess drip; press into breadcrumbs to coat evenly. Rest 5 minutes.
Heat 1/2 inch frying oil in a wide skillet over medium to medium-high heat to 350°F.
Fry 1–2 cutlets at a time without crowding until deeply golden and cooked through, about 2–3 minutes per side; internal temp 165°F.
Transfer to a rack or paper towels; season lightly with a pinch of salt while hot. Repeat, keeping oil at 325–350°F.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges; sprinkle with parsley just before serving.
tip: Use very fresh, fine dry breadcrumbs for best crispness; avoid panko. Keep cutlets thin and oil hot for proper blistered crust. Leftovers re-crisp in a 375°F oven for 8–10 minutes.

title: Chicken Paprikash
ing: 2 lb bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks
8 oz egg noodles, cooked for serving
steps: Pat chicken dry; season both sides with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wide pot over medium-high; brown chicken skin-side down 5 to 7 minutes, flip and brown 3 minutes. Transfer to a plate.

Reduce heat to medium. Add butter and onions; cook, stirring, until soft and pale gold, 10 to 12 minutes. Stir in garlic; cook 30 seconds. Remove pot from heat; stir in sweet and hot paprika until onions are brick red.

Return pot to medium heat. Add broth and water; scrape up browned bits. Nestle chicken, skin-side up; bring to a simmer. Cover and cook gently for 30 minutes, then uncover and simmer 10 minutes more, until chicken reaches 175°F.
Transfer chicken to a warm plate. Boil sauce over medium-high to reduce slightly, 5 minutes. In a bowl, whisk sour cream with flour until smooth and lump-free.

Off heat, whisk 1/2 cup hot sauce into sour cream mixture to temper. Return mixture to pot, whisking until velvety. Simmer gently over low 2 to 3 minutes; do not boil. Adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Return chicken to the pot, spoon with sauce, and warm 2 minutes over low. Meanwhile, cook egg noodles per package in salted water; drain well.
Serve chicken and generous paprika-cream sauce over noodles. Garnish with parsley and a final spoon of sauce.
tip: Use only fresh, vibrant Hungarian paprika for best color and sweetness. Can be cooled and refrigerated 2 days; rewarm gently without boiling to prevent curdling.

title: Poule au Pot
ing: 2 leeks, white and light green parts, cleaned
6 oz vermicelli or thin egg noodles
2 tbsp chopped parsley, for garnish, to taste
steps: Pat chicken dry, season with 2 tsp salt and 1 tsp pepper. Heat frying oil in a large pot over medium; brown chicken lightly on all sides for 6–8 minutes to deepen flavor.
Add 8 cups water to the pot, bring to a gentle boil, then skim foam thoroughly for 5–7 minutes until broth runs clear.
Tie parsley, thyme, and bay leaf in a bundle. Add herb bundle, onion, leeks (halved), carrots (chunked), celery (chunked), and turnip (chunked). Reduce to a bare simmer.
Cover and simmer gently for 70–90 minutes, adjusting heat to keep a quiet bubble, until chicken reaches 165°F in the thigh and vegetables are tender.
Lift chicken to a platter, tent loosely 10 minutes. Strain broth; reserve vegetables warm. Return clear broth to the pot and bring to a simmer.
Add vermicelli to the simmering broth; cook for 5–7 minutes until just tender. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste.
Carve chicken into leg, thigh, and breast pieces, keeping skin intact. Slice vegetables into neat lengths for serving.
Serve chicken and vegetables in warm bowls. Ladle hot noodle broth over, and pass Dijon mustard at table; garnish with chopped parsley to taste.
tip: Swap vermicelli with rice; simmer 15 minutes before serving. Chill leftovers in broth up to 3 days; reheat gently to avoid drying the chicken.

title: Chicken Fricassée
ing: 2 lb bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks
2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: Pat chicken dry and season with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil and 1 tbsp butter in a wide Dutch oven over medium-high until shimmering, 2 minutes.
Brown chicken skin-side down until deep golden, 5 to 7 minutes; flip and brown 3 minutes more. Work in batches, adding oil as needed. Transfer to a plate; pour off all but 1 tbsp fat.
Add mushrooms and cook over medium, stirring, until they release moisture and take color, 6 to 8 minutes. Add onion and cook until translucent, 4 minutes; stir in garlic for 30 seconds.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables; cook, stirring, 1 minute. Pour in wine, scraping browned bits; simmer 2 minutes. Whisk in chicken stock; bring to a gentle simmer.
Return chicken and accumulated juices, skin-side up. Cover and simmer gently over low heat until chicken reaches 175°F in the thickest thigh, 25 to 30 minutes.
Transfer chicken to a warm plate. Skim surface fat. Stir in cream and thyme; simmer uncovered over medium-low until slightly thickened and glossy, 5 to 7 minutes.
Off heat, stir in lemon juice. Taste and adjust salt and pepper. Return chicken to sauce and warm 2 minutes over low heat.
Serve chicken napped with sauce; garnish with chopped parsley. Accompany with buttered noodles, rice, or potatoes.
tip: For a richer finish, temper in 2 egg yolks with the hot sauce off heat. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; rewarm gently without boiling to prevent the sauce from breaking.

title: Coronation Chicken
ing: 1 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish
steps: Place chicken in a saucepan, cover with 4 cups water and 1 tsp salt, bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then poach until internal temperature reaches 165°F, about 12–15 minutes. Cool and dice.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add onion and cook until soft and translucent, 6–8 minutes. Stir in garlic, curry powder, and tomato paste; cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken stock and apricot jam, simmer for 3–4 minutes to make a glossy, slightly syrupy sauce. Remove from heat and cool to room temperature, 10 minutes.
In a large bowl whisk mayonnaise, yogurt, and lemon juice. Stir in the cooled curry-onion sauce until smooth and well combined.
Fold in diced chicken and chopped raisins until evenly coated. Taste and adjust seasoning with a pinch of salt and pepper to taste.
Chill the coronation chicken for at least 15 minutes before serving. Garnish with toasted almonds and chopped cilantro. Serve in sandwiches or with crisp lettuce and rice salad.
tip: Swap golden raisins for chopped dried apricots. Make ahead: keeps covered in the fridge up to 2 days; stir in a spoon of yogurt to loosen before serving.

title: Cock-a-Leekie Soup
ing: 6 leeks, white and light green parts only, cleaned and sliced
1/2 tsp black pepper, or to taste
1 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: Warm a large pot over medium heat and add a thin film of oil. Add chicken thighs skin-side down and brown lightly for 5 minutes to develop flavor.
Pour in 8 cups water, bring to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Skim foam, cover partially, and simmer for 30 minutes.
Stir in barley and continue to simmer for 20 minutes, skimming as needed. Maintain a gentle simmer, not a rolling boil.
Add sliced leeks and prunes. Simmer until leeks are tender and barley is soft, about 20 minutes.
Transfer chicken to a board. When cool enough to handle, discard skin and bones, shred the meat, and return it to the pot.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Simmer 5 minutes more to meld flavors.
Ladle into warm bowls and garnish with chopped parsley. Serve hot.
tip: For clearer broth, strain before adding leeks and prunes. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; reheat gently, adding a splash of water if thickened.

title: Chicken Souvlaki
ing: 1 1/2 lb chicken thighs, trimmed and 1 1/2-inch cubed
1/2 cup plain Greek yogurt, for serving
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for serving
8 oz cherry tomatoes, for optional skewering or side
steps: Soak 8 wooden skewers in water for 20 minutes. In a bowl, whisk 1/4 cup olive oil, 3 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp red wine vinegar, fresh and dried oregano, garlic, lemon zest, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Add chicken cubes to the marinade, toss to coat, cover, and refrigerate for 20 to 30 minutes (or up to 2 hours for deeper flavor).
Thread chicken onto soaked skewers, packing pieces snugly but not overly tight; optionally alternate with cherry tomatoes.
Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high (about 400°F). Oil grates lightly. Grill skewers 8 to 10 minutes total, turning every 2 to 3 minutes, until browned and juices run clear.
Check doneness: chicken must reach 165°F at the thickest piece. If needed, continue grilling 1 to 2 minutes per side.
Rest skewers 3 minutes. In a small bowl, mix 1/2 cup yogurt with 1 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt and pepper to make a quick sauce.
Serve souvlaki hot with lemon wedges for squeezing, yogurt sauce, and warmed pita or a simple salad if desired.
tip: Substitute boneless skinless breasts cut to the same size; watch time to avoid drying. Marinated, uncooked skewers keep 1 day refrigerated; cooked leftovers keep 3 days.

title: Chicken Gyros
ing: 1.5 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, trimmed
steps: Whisk 1/2 cup yogurt, olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, coriander, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Add chicken, coat well, cover, and marinate 30 minutes (or up to 12 hours) refrigerated.
Make tzatziki: combine remaining 1/2 cup yogurt with squeezed cucumber, dill, red wine vinegar, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Chill until serving.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high and add frying oil as needed. Shake excess marinade and sear chicken 5 to 6 minutes per side until browned and juices run clear.
Check doneness: cook chicken to an internal 165°F. Transfer to a board, rest 5 minutes, then slice thinly across the grain.
Warm pitas in a dry skillet over medium or in a 350°F oven for 3 to 5 minutes until pliable.
Assemble gyros: spread tzatziki on warm pita, add sliced chicken, tomato, red onion, and lettuce.
Fold pita around fillings and serve immediately while warm.
tip: For a charred edge, broil sliced cooked chicken on a sheet pan 2 to 3 minutes. Swap thighs with boneless breasts, but watch doneness closely to avoid drying; marinate at least 1 hour for best flavor.

title: Chakhokhbili
ing: 2 lb chicken thighs, bone-in skinless, cut into large chunks
1/2 cup fresh basil (purple or sweet), chopped
1/2 cup water or low-sodium chicken stock
steps: Pat chicken dry and season lightly with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a heavy pot over medium-high, add chicken in a single layer, and brown 4 to 5 minutes per side; work in batches and add oil as needed.
Reduce heat to medium, add sliced onion to the pot drippings, and cook, stirring, until softened and lightly golden, about 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in garlic, ground coriander, paprika, and chili flakes; cook 30 seconds until fragrant. Add chopped tomatoes and any juices; scrape up browned bits.
Return chicken to the pot with 1/2 cup water or stock. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently over low heat for 25 minutes, stirring once.
Uncover and continue to simmer until chicken is tender and sauce thickens and glistens, about 10 to 15 minutes; adjust salt and pepper. Ensure chicken reaches 165°F.
Stir in most of the cilantro, parsley, and basil, reserving a little for garnish; simmer 2 minutes to meld flavors, then remove from heat.
Rest 5 minutes. Garnish with remaining herbs and serve hot with flatbread or rice.
tip: For a sharper note, add 1 to 2 tbsp dry white wine or 1 tsp red wine vinegar with the tomatoes. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; reheat gently, adding a splash of water if thick.

title: Shkmeruli (Garlic Chicken)
ing: 1 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: Pat chicken dry, spatchcock it by removing backbone, and season all over with 2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Let stand at room temperature for 15 minutes while you prepare the pan.
Heat 2 tbsp frying oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Place chicken skin side down and press with a weight; sear until deep golden, about 7 to 9 minutes.
Flip chicken skin side up and transfer skillet to a 425°F oven. Roast until juices run clear and thickest breast reaches 165°F, about 20 to 25 minutes. Transfer chicken to a plate; tent loosely.
Return skillet to medium-low. Add butter, then garlic; stir just until fragrant, about 30 seconds—do not brown. Stir in milk and water, scraping up browned bits; simmer for 3 to 4 minutes to meld.
Taste sauce; add a pinch of salt if needed. Return chicken skin side up to the skillet. Spoon sauce over and simmer gently on low for 2 to 3 minutes to rewarm and coat.
Cut chicken into serving pieces. Spoon plenty of garlicky sauce over and scatter parsley on top. Serve immediately with crusty bread for dipping.
tip: For a village-style touch, use a clay ketsi if you have one. To reheat, warm chicken pieces in the sauce over low heat, adding a splash of water or milk to loosen if needed.

title: Shish Tawook
ing: 2 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
1 large yellow onion, cut into 1 1/2-inch chunks
1 large red bell pepper, cut into 1 1/2-inch chunks
steps: Soak 8 wooden skewers in water for 30 minutes to prevent burning. Prepare a grill for medium-high heat, 400–450°F.
Whisk yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, salt, paprika, coriander, cumin, cinnamon, black pepper, tomato paste, and vinegar in a large bowl until smooth.
Add chicken to the bowl and toss to coat evenly. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for 30–60 minutes; for best flavor, marinate 4 hours (within the total time, use 60 minutes).
Thread chicken onto soaked skewers, alternating with onion and bell pepper, ending with chicken to secure. Discard used marinade.
Oil the grill grates lightly. Grill skewers over direct heat, covered, turning every 3–4 minutes, until lightly charred, 10–12 minutes total.
Move to indirect heat and cook until chicken reaches 165°F at the thickest piece, 3–5 minutes more. Rest skewers 5 minutes off heat.
Optional: Warm pita on the grill for 30–60 seconds per side. Serve with toum or lemon wedges.
tip: For juicier bites, swap half the breasts with chicken thighs. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; reheat gently or serve room temp in wraps.

title: Musakhan
ing: 4 rounds taboon or thick pita bread (8–9 inch)
steps: Pat chicken dry, then toss with 2 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp sumac, allspice, cumin, coriander, 1 tsp kosher salt, and 1/2 tsp black pepper; marinate 20 minutes while you prep onions.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium; add onions and 1/2 tsp salt, cook until very soft and pale golden, 12–15 minutes, stirring often so they wilt without browning.
Stir in chicken stock and lemon juice; simmer for 2 minutes, then remove from heat. Taste and adjust salt. Reserve half of the onion mixture for topping later; keep warm.
Arrange marinated chicken skin-side up on a rimmed sheet; roast at 425°F for 35–40 minutes until skin is crisp and thickest part reaches 165°F.

While chicken roasts, warm taboon or thick pita on a dry skillet over medium for 1–2 minutes per side until pliable. Brush each with remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, then spread with the remaining warm onions.
Set chicken on the onion-topped breads; spoon any pan juices over. Scatter the reserved onions on top and sprinkle toasted pine nuts and a pinch of sumac if desired.
Return assembled breads to the oven at 400°F for 5–7 minutes to meld flavors and lightly crisp edges. Garnish with chopped parsley and serve immediately.
tip: Taboon bread is traditional; thick pita or naan works well. Toast pine nuts in a dry skillet 3–4 minutes. Leftovers keep 2 days refrigerated; rewarm at 350°F until hot.

title: Chicken Tagine with Olives and Preserved Lemon
ing: 2 lb bone-in chicken thighs, skin on, trimmed
1 preserved lemon, rind only, rinsed and sliced
1/4 cup fresh cilantro, chopped, plus more for garnish as needed
steps: In a bowl, combine garlic, ginger, turmeric, cumin, coriander, saffron, pepper, salt, 2 tbsp olive oil, and lemon juice to form a paste. Rub paste over chicken and marinate for 20 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a tagine or heavy Dutch oven over medium heat for 2 minutes. Add onions and cook, stirring, until softened and lightly golden, about 8 minutes.
Nestle chicken skin side down over onions and sear until skin is lightly browned, about 4 minutes. Flip chicken, add broth, and scatter cilantro and parsley over.
Cover with lid and reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 35 minutes, maintaining a gentle bubble; do not boil vigorously.
Stir in olives and preserved lemon rind. Re-cover and simmer until chicken reaches 165°F at the thickest part and is very tender, 10 to 15 minutes.
Uncover and simmer 3 to 5 minutes to slightly reduce sauce until glossy and spoonable. Skim excess fat if desired.
Taste and adjust seasoning with a pinch of salt or a squeeze of lemon if needed. Rest off heat 3 minutes.
Serve hot, sprinkled with chopped cilantro as needed, with couscous or crusty bread.
tip: Swap green olives with a mix of green and purple olives for depth. The stew improves overnight; chill up to 3 days and rewarm gently, adding a splash of water if the sauce thickens.

title: Chicken Bastilla
ing: 1 lb bone-in chicken thighs, skin removed
1 lb bone-in chicken drumsticks, skin removed
1 cup whole almonds, toasted, roughly chopped
steps: Pat chicken dry and season with 1/2 tsp salt and black pepper. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wide pot over medium-high, brown chicken 6 to 8 minutes, turning until golden.
Add onion, garlic, ginger, turmeric, 1 tsp cinnamon, saffron, and remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Stir, cover, and cook over medium-low until chicken is tender, 30 to 35 minutes, stirring once or twice.
Transfer chicken to a plate. Boil the sauce over medium to reduce to a thick jammy mixture, 6 to 8 minutes. Off heat, stir in cilantro and parsley.

When cool enough, remove chicken skin and bones, shred meat finely. Return pot to low heat, add beaten eggs to the onion mixture, and stir constantly until softly set and moist, 3 to 4 minutes. Cool completely.
Mix almonds with 1/4 cup sugar and 1 tsp cinnamon; set aside. Heat oven to 375°F. Brush a 9-inch pie pan with melted butter.

Layer 4 phyllo sheets in the pan, one at a time, brushing each with butter and rotating so edges overhang evenly. Spread half the almond mixture, then all shredded chicken, then the egg-onion mixture, then remaining almonds.
Fold phyllo over filling to enclose. Top with 4 more buttered phyllo sheets, tucking edges down the sides. Brush top with remaining butter and slash a few vents.
Bake at 375°F until deep golden and crisp, 28 to 35 minutes. Rest 10 minutes, then dust with powdered sugar and cinnamon before slicing and serving warm.
tip: Phyllo dries fast; keep sheets covered with a damp towel while working. Bastilla can be assembled a day ahead and baked from cold, adding 5 minutes to the bake time.

title: Chicken Yassa
ing: 2 tbsp neutral frying oil, as needed
2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: Whisk 1/2 cup lemon juice, 1/4 cup mustard, 4 cloves garlic, 1 tsp red pepper flakes, 1 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp vinegar, 1/2 tsp pepper, and 1/2 tsp salt. Toss with 2 lb chicken and 2 sliced onions. Marinate 30 minutes to 2 hours refrigerated.
Remove chicken and onions from marinade, reserving all liquids and onions. Pat chicken dry and season lightly with salt. Blot onions if very wet to encourage browning.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high. Sear chicken skin-side down until deep golden, about 4 to 5 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
Add the marinated onions to the pot. Cook, stirring, until softened and caramelized at edges, 10 to 12 minutes. Do not burn; reduce heat if needed.
Return chicken to pot. Stir in reserved marinade, 1 cup chicken broth, 1 bay leaf, and lemon rounds. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Cover and simmer gently for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until chicken is tender and reaches 165°F at the thickest part.
Uncover and simmer 5 to 8 minutes to thicken to a glossy sauce that coats a spoon. Adjust salt, pepper, and lemon to taste.
Discard bay leaf. Serve hot over steamed rice, garnish with chopped parsley.
tip: For a smokier, classic touch, grill or broil the chicken to char before simmering. Yassa improves overnight; chill up to 3 days and reheat gently, loosening with broth if needed.

title: Doro Wat
ing: 2 lb chicken drumsticks and thighs, skin-on, bone-in
1 cup red onion, very finely minced
1 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
1/2 tsp black pepper, or to taste
2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish
steps: Score chicken pieces, pat dry, and marinate with 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1/4 tsp pepper for 15 minutes while you prep aromatics.
In a heavy pot over medium heat, dry-sweat 1 cup minced onion with a pinch of salt, stirring often until deep brick-red and very soft, about 15 to 18 minutes; add a splash of water if scorching.
Stir in niter kibbeh and 2 tbsp frying oil; add garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant, 2 minutes. Add berbere and cook, stirring, 1 to 2 minutes to bloom the spices.
Add tomato paste and cook 2 minutes. Stir in chicken stock and bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat.
Nestle chicken into the sauce skin side down, cover, and simmer for 35 minutes, turning once, until the thickest part reaches 165°F; reduce heat if needed to maintain a gentle simmer.
Meanwhile, prick eggs once with a pin, place in cold water, bring to a boil, then simmer 9 minutes. Shock in ice water, peel, and score eggs lightly to help sauce cling.
Uncover stew, add sliced onion and peeled eggs, and simmer uncovered for 10 to 12 minutes to thicken and glaze the chicken; adjust salt and pepper to taste, and finish with remaining lemon juice.
Rest 5 minutes off heat. Serve hot with injera, spooning sauce over, and garnish with cilantro.
tip: Use good berbere and niter kibbeh for authentic flavor; ghee + a pinch of fenugreek and cardamom works in a pinch. Leftovers keep 3 days chilled; rewarm gently with a splash of stock.

title: Peri-Peri Chicken
ing: 3 lb bone-in chicken pieces, patted dry
1 oz dried African bird’s eye chiles, crushed
2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: Make the peri-peri paste: In a bowl, whisk garlic, lemon juice, red wine vinegar, olive oil, smoked and sweet paprika, salt, pepper, oregano, sugar, lemon zest, and crushed dried bird’s eye chiles until thick.

Marinate the chicken: Coat chicken thoroughly with the paste, lifting skin where possible. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, preferably 4 hours; bring to room temperature for 20 minutes before cooking.
Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a sheet pan with foil and set a rack over it. Brush rack lightly with frying oil to prevent sticking.
Roast the chicken skin-side up at 425°F for 25 minutes. Baste with pan juices and remaining marinade, then continue roasting 15–20 minutes until the thickest part reads 165°F.
Optional char: For classic blistered edges, broil on high for 2–3 minutes, watching closely until the skin is lightly charred in spots.
Rest the chicken 5–10 minutes on the rack so juices settle and skin stays crisp.
Serve hot with any pan juices spooned over, lemon wedges for squeezing, and parsley sprinkled on top.
tip: Swap dried bird’s eye chiles with dried cayenne flakes if needed; adjust heat cautiously. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; rewarm at 350°F for 10–12 minutes to re-crisp skin.

title: Jerk Chicken
ing: 3 lb bone-in chicken pieces, skin-on (legs and thighs)
steps: Make the marinade: In a blender, combine scallions, garlic, ginger, thyme, Scotch bonnets, allspice, nutmeg, cinnamon, brown sugar, soy sauce, lime juice, and vegetable oil; blend until smooth, 30 to 60 seconds.
Score the chicken skin lightly with a knife. Pat dry, season with salt and black pepper, then rub with all the marinade, working under skin where possible.
Marinate covered in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, preferably 8 to 12 hours; bring to room temperature for 20 minutes before grilling.
Prepare a charcoal or gas grill for two-zone cooking at medium heat (about 350°F to 375°F). For extra authenticity, add pimento (allspice) wood or soaked wood chips to the coals.
Grill chicken skin-side down over indirect heat with the lid closed, turning every 10 minutes, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part reads 165°F, about 40 to 50 minutes.
For a charred finish, move pieces over direct heat and sear 1 to 2 minutes per side until skin is well browned and lightly blistered; avoid excessive flare-ups.
Rest chicken on a platter, tented, for 5 minutes to retain juices. Spoon any accumulated juices over the chicken.
Serve hot with rice and peas and festival or hard dough bread; offer lime wedges on the side.
tip: For milder heat, replace one Scotch bonnet with a small sweet pepper. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; reheat covered at 325°F until warmed through, or shred for sandwiches.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
ing: 1.5 lb boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1.5-inch pieces
steps: Marinate chicken: In a bowl, combine yogurt, lemon juice, 1 tbsp garam masala, 1 tsp cumin, paprika, coriander, 1 tsp salt, and pepper. Add chicken, coat well, cover, and chill for 30 to 60 minutes.
Prepare aromatics: Heat 1 tbsp oil and butter in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add onion and cook until golden, 8 to 10 minutes. Stir in garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Bloom spices: Add turmeric, remaining 1 tbsp garam masala, remaining 1 tsp cumin, and Kashmiri chili. Cook, stirring, 30 seconds to bloom the spices.
Build sauce: Stir in crushed tomatoes, water, and sugar. Bring to a simmer, then cook uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Sear chicken: Heat a broiler to high (or grill to medium-high). Thread chicken on a rack-lined tray brushed with oil. Broil 6 to 8 minutes, turning once, until lightly charred and 160°F.
Finish masala: Slide seared chicken and any juices into the sauce. Simmer gently for 5 minutes until chicken reaches 165°F and is tender.
Enrich and season: Stir in heavy cream; simmer 2 minutes. Season with salt to taste. If too thick, loosen with a splash of water.
Serve: Rest 2 minutes. Garnish with cilantro and serve hot with basmati rice or naan.
tip: For a lighter sauce, swap half-and-half for cream. Marinate the chicken up to 24 hours; the flavor deepens. Leftovers keep refrigerated 3 days; reheat gently, thinning with water if needed.

title: Butter Chicken
ing: 1.5 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
steps: Combine yogurt, lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chili, cumin, coriander, garam masala, and salt; add chicken and coat well. Marinate 30 minutes at room temp or up to 8 hours chilled.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high. Shake excess marinade and sear chicken in two batches until lightly charred, 3–4 minutes per side; set aside. Chicken will finish cooking in sauce.
In the same pan, melt 2 tbsp butter over medium. Add tomato puree and sugar; cook, stirring, until thick and glossy, 6–8 minutes to reduce raw taste.
Stir in water and bring to a simmer. Add seared chicken and any juices; simmer gently over medium-low until chicken reaches 165°F and is tender, 8–10 minutes.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in cream, remaining 1 tbsp butter, crushed fenugreek leaves, and black pepper. Simmer for 2 minutes; adjust salt and chili to taste.
Rest off heat 3 minutes for flavors to meld. Garnish with cilantro and a drizzle of cream. Serve hot with naan or steamed basmati rice.
