tip: Swap Kashmiri chili with 1 tsp paprika + 1/2 tsp cayenne. Sauce improves overnight; chill up to 3 days or freeze 1 month. Rewarm gently, adding a splash of water or cream.

title: Chicken Biryani
ing: 1 1/2 lb bone-in chicken pieces, skin removed
2 cups basmati rice, rinsed and soaked 30 minutes
1 tbsp whole spices (6 green cardamom, 6 cloves, 1 bay leaf, 1-inch cinnamon)
2 tbsp neutral frying oil, as needed
1/4 cup warm milk, with a pinch of saffron
steps: Marinate: In a bowl combine yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, crushed fried onions, mint, cilantro, chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, 2 tsp salt, and lemon juice. Add chicken, coat well, cover, and refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Parboil rice: Bring 10 cups water to a rolling boil with 1 1/2 tsp salt, whole spices, and cumin. Add soaked rice and boil until 70% cooked, 5 to 6 minutes. Drain immediately and spread to steam-dry for 2 minutes.

Sear aromatics: Heat 1 tbsp ghee and 1 tbsp oil in a heavy 4- to 5-qt pot over medium-high. Add marinated chicken in a single layer; cook 3 minutes per side to lightly sear, do not fully cook. Remove pot from heat.

Layer: Return chicken to pot in an even layer with all its marinade. Top with half the parboiled rice, sprinkle half the saffron milk and half the fried onions. Add remaining rice, saffron milk, and 1 tbsp ghee. Dot with 1 tbsp oil if dry.
Seal for dum: Cover the pot with a tight lid. For a loose lid, seal rim with a simple flour-water dough rope or wrap lid with foil to trap steam.
Steam (dum): Set pot over the lowest burner heat. Cook for 25 minutes until steam escapes steadily and internal chicken temperature reaches 165°F. Rest off heat, covered, for 10 minutes.
Finish: Gently fluff from the edges, lifting rice without breaking grains and turning pieces to coat in juices. Discard whole spices as found.
Serve: Plate biryani with a scatter of cilantro and reserved fried onions. Offer raita and lemon wedges alongside.
tip: Use store-bought fried onions to save time. To make ahead, marinate chicken up to 12 hours; parboil rice just before layering so grains stay distinct.

title: Chicken Korma
ing: 1.5 lb bone-in chicken thighs, skin removed
1/2 cup raw cashews, soaked 20 minutes, drained
1/4 cup blanched almonds, soaked 20 minutes, drained
steps: Marinate chicken with yogurt, lemon juice, 1 tsp salt, and turmeric; cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes while you prep other ingredients.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee and 1 tbsp oil in a heavy pot over medium; add onions and cook, stirring, until deep golden, 15–18 minutes. Remove half for garnish; keep the rest in pot.
Add garlic and ginger; sauté 1 minute. Add coriander, cumin, cardamom, and chili powder; stir 30 seconds until fragrant.
Blend soaked cashews and almonds with 1/2 cup stock to a smooth paste. Add paste to pot; cook, stirring, 2–3 minutes until it thickens and ghee separates.
Add marinated chicken with all marinade; cook over medium-high, stirring, until opaque on the outside, 4–5 minutes.
Stir in remaining 1/2 cup stock, raisins, and sugar; bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook on low until chicken reaches 175°F at the thickest part, 20–25 minutes.
Uncover; stir in nutmeg, black pepper, remaining 1 tbsp ghee, and heavy cream. Simmer uncovered 3–5 minutes until the sauce coats the back of a spoon. Adjust salt to taste.
Rest 5 minutes off heat. Garnish with reserved fried onions and cilantro; serve hot with steamed basmati rice or naan.
tip: Sub 1/2 cup canned coconut milk for cream for a lactose-light version. Korma tastes better the next day; refrigerate up to 3 days and rewarm gently with a splash of stock.

title: Chicken Vindaloo
ing: 2 lb bone-in chicken thighs, skin removed, cut into 2-inch pieces
8 dried Kashmiri red chilies, stems removed
steps: Make the spice paste: Toast cumin seeds, coriander seeds, mustard seeds, and cloves in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes until fragrant; cool, then grind to a powder.

Soak Kashmiri chilies in 1/2 cup hot water for 10 minutes. Blend chilies with soaking liquid, ground spices, garlic, ginger, turmeric, cinnamon, vinegar, tamarind paste, jaggery, salt, and pepper to a smooth paste.
Marinate chicken: Toss chicken with 2/3 of the paste in a bowl, cover, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (up to 8 hours) to season deeply.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add onions and cook, stirring, until deeply golden, 10 to 12 minutes; add remaining oil if needed.
Add remaining vindaloo paste to onions and fry for 2 minutes until the oil separates and the paste darkens slightly, stirring constantly to avoid scorching.
Add marinated chicken and any juices; sear 4 to 5 minutes, turning to coat well. Add 1 cup water, bring to a boil, then reduce to a lively simmer, cover, and cook for 25 minutes.
Uncover and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes more to thicken. Stir occasionally until sauce is glossy and chicken is tender and reaches 165°F at the thickest part.
Rest 5 minutes. Adjust salt, jaggery, or vinegar to balance heat, tang, and sweetness. Garnish with cilantro and serve hot with steamed rice or warm flatbread.
tip: Kashmiri chilies give heat and color; sub 2 tbsp Kashmiri chili powder if needed. Tastes even better the next day—cool, refrigerate up to 3 days, and rewarm gently with a splash of water.

title: Chicken Jalfrezi
ing: 1.5 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 tbsp neutral frying oil, as needed
1 green bell pepper, cut into 1-inch strips
1 red bell pepper, cut into 1-inch strips
steps: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high until shimmering, then add cumin seeds and bloom for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add onion and sauté over medium-high, stirring, until edges are deeply golden, 7 to 9 minutes. Stir in ginger and garlic; cook 1 minute.
Add ground cumin, coriander, turmeric, and Kashmiri chili; fry 30 seconds. Stir in tomato puree; cook down until glossy and thick, 3 to 4 minutes.
Increase heat to high; add chicken in a single layer. Sear without moving 2 minutes, then stir-fry until opaque on the outside, 3 minutes.
Add bell peppers and tomato wedges; stir-fry on high so liquids evaporate and vegetables stay crisp-tender, 4 to 5 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium; season with salt and pepper. Cover and cook, stirring once, until chicken reaches 165°F, about 4 to 6 minutes.
Uncover; sprinkle garam masala and lime juice. Toss over high heat to glaze and lightly char edges, 1 to 2 minutes. Adjust seasoning to taste.
Rest 2 minutes off heat, then garnish with cilantro and serve hot with naan or steamed basmati rice.
tip: Substitute Kashmiri chili with 1/2 tsp paprika + pinch cayenne. Leftovers keep 3 days chilled; reheat over medium-high to revive the stir-fry char.

title: Chicken Karahi
ing: 2 lb bone-in chicken, cut into medium pieces
2 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped, plus more for garnish
2 tbsp green chilies, thinly sliced, for garnish
1 tsp fresh ginger, julienned, for garnish
steps: Heat 3 tbsp oil in a heavy karahi or wok over medium-high until shimmering, 2 minutes. Add onion and sauté until just golden at the edges, 6–8 minutes.
Add chicken and sear, stirring, until opaque and lightly browned, 6–8 minutes. Add garlic and ginger; cook until fragrant, 1 minute.
Stir in chili powder, coriander, cumin, salt, and pepper; cook the spices in the oil for 30 seconds to bloom.
Add tomatoes and increase heat to high; cook, stirring, until tomatoes break down and release juices, 6–8 minutes.
Reduce to medium; cook uncovered, stirring often, until the gravy thickens and oil separates at the edges, 8–10 minutes.
Stir in yogurt over medium heat and cook until glossy and clinging to chicken, 3–4 minutes. Ensure chicken reaches 165°F in the thickest pieces.
Fold in cilantro and half the green chilies and ginger. Simmer 2 minutes to meld flavors, then adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Rest off heat 2 minutes. Garnish with remaining green chilies, ginger, and cilantro. Serve hot with naan or steamed basmati rice.
tip: Sub 1 tsp crushed dried fenugreek leaves for extra aroma. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; rewarm gently with a splash of water to loosen the gravy.

title: Chicken 65
ing: 1 lb boneless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 tbsp vinegar, white or apple cider
steps: In a bowl, mix yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri chili powder, pepper, cumin, coriander, turmeric, rice flour, cornstarch, salt, lemon juice, soy sauce, and vinegar to form a thick marinade.
Add chicken pieces, coat thoroughly, and rest for 20 minutes at room temperature (or up to 4 hours refrigerated).
Heat 1 1/2 inches frying oil in a deep skillet to 350°F. Fry chicken in batches 4–5 minutes until deep red and cooked through to 165°F internal; drain on a rack.
Pour off most frying oil, leaving 2 tbsp in the pan. Heat over medium, add mustard seeds; let them splutter for 20 seconds.
Add curry leaves and slit green chilies; sauté 30–40 seconds until fragrant.
Sprinkle in sugar and add 2 tbsp water to create a light glaze; toss to combine for 20 seconds.
Add fried chicken to the pan; toss over medium-high heat for 1–2 minutes to coat evenly and re-crisp.
Garnish with cilantro and serve hot with lemon wedges; rest 2 minutes before serving to set the crust.
tip: For extra heat, add 1/2 tsp crushed red chili to the marinade. To bake: brush marinated pieces with oil and bake at 425°F for 15–18 min, then pan-toss with the tempering.

title: Chicken Tikka
ing: 1.75 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, trimmed and 1.5-inch chunks
steps: Whisk yogurt, lemon juice, ginger-garlic paste, oil, Kashmiri chili, coriander, cumin, garam masala, paprika, salt, turmeric, and pepper until smooth, about 1 minute.
Add chicken and red onion, toss to coat, cover, and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour (up to 12 hours) for best flavor.
Thread chicken and onion onto soaked skewers, packing pieces snugly but not tight. Rest at room temperature for 15 minutes while heating grill.
Preheat a gas grill to medium-high (about 425°F) or prepare a hot charcoal fire with a two-zone setup; oil grates just before grilling.
Grill skewers over direct heat, turning every 2 to 3 minutes, until lightly charred, 8 to 10 minutes total.
Move to indirect heat, baste lightly with melted ghee, and cook covered until chicken reaches 165°F internal temperature, 4 to 6 minutes more.
Transfer to a platter, rest 5 minutes, then squeeze lemon over and sprinkle with cilantro to taste.
Serve hot with onion, lemon wedges, and optional green chutney or naan.
tip: Use Kashmiri chili for color and gentle heat; swap with 1 tsp hot paprika + 1 tsp sweet paprika if needed. Marinate up to 12 hours; leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated, reheat covered at 300°F.

title: Chicken Xacuti
ing: 2 lb bone-in chicken, cut into 10 pieces
6 dried Kashmiri red chilies, stems removed
steps: Marinate chicken with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp turmeric from the measured turmeric; set aside for 20 minutes while you prep.
Dry-roast chilies, coriander, cumin, peppercorns, poppy and fennel seeds in a skillet over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant; remove to cool.
In same skillet, toast grated coconut over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes until golden; add nutmeg in last 30 seconds. Cool.
Heat 1 tbsp oil over medium; sauté onions for 10 minutes until deep golden. Reserve half for garnish; leave half in pan.
Blend roasted spices, toasted coconut, sautéed onions (half left in pan), garlic, ginger, remaining turmeric, tamarind, and 3/4 cup water to a smooth paste.
Add 1 tbsp oil to the pan, pour in the spice paste, and fry over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring, until it releases oil and darkens.
Add chicken and 1/4 cup water; stir to coat. Cover and simmer over medium-low for 25 to 30 minutes until chicken reaches 165°F and is tender.
Stir in coconut milk and reserved onions; simmer for 5 minutes to meld. Adjust salt to taste and thin with a splash of water if needed. Rest 5 minutes.
Garnish with cilantro and serve hot with Goan pao or steamed rice.
tip: Swap Kashmiri chilies with mild paprika plus a few arbol for heat. Curry keeps 3 days refrigerated; flavor improves overnight. Thin with water when reheating to preserve the silky gravy.

title: Kerala Chicken Curry
ing: 2 lb bone-in chicken thighs, cut into 2-inch pieces
steps: Warm 2 tbsp coconut oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Add 2 sprigs curry leaves and 1 cup sliced onion; cook, stirring, until deep golden, 10 to 12 minutes.

Stir in 1 tbsp grated ginger and 5 minced garlic cloves; sauté until fragrant, 45 to 60 seconds. Add 2 tsp Kashmiri chili, 1 tsp coriander, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp pepper, and 1/2 tsp crushed fennel; fry 30 seconds.
Add 1 cup chopped tomato and 1/2 tsp salt; cook, stirring, until tomatoes break down and oil separates at the edges, 5 to 7 minutes.
Add 2 lb chicken pieces; toss to coat in masala and cook until surfaces turn opaque, 4 to 5 minutes.
Pour in 1 cup thin coconut milk and 1/2 cup water; bring to a boil, then reduce heat to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until chicken reaches 165°F, 18 to 22 minutes.
Uncover and simmer to slightly thicken, 3 to 5 minutes. Stir in 1/2 cup thick coconut milk and 1 tsp white vinegar; simmer on low for 2 minutes. Adjust salt to taste.
Turn off heat, rest 5 minutes for flavors to meld. Garnish with 1 tbsp chopped cilantro and a few fresh curry leaves if desired. Serve hot with steamed rice or appam.
tip: Swap chicken thighs with drumsticks if preferred. Curry keeps 3 days refrigerated; reheat gently without boiling to prevent coconut milk from splitting.

title: Chicken Saag
ing: 1 1/2 lb chicken thighs, boneless skinless, cut into 1-inch cubes
2 tbsp cilantro, chopped, for garnish, as needed
steps: Blanch greens: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add spinach and cook for 1 minute. Drain, shock in ice water, squeeze dry, then blend with 1/2 cup water to a coarse puree.
Marinate chicken: In a bowl, combine yogurt, 1/2 tsp salt, half the ginger, and half the garlic. Add chicken, coat well, and rest for 15 minutes while you start the sauce.
Build masala: Heat 3 tbsp ghee in a heavy pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and sizzle 30 seconds. Stir in onion and cook until golden, 8–10 minutes.

Add aromatics and spices: Add remaining ginger and garlic; cook 1 minute. Stir in coriander, ground cumin, turmeric, and Kashmiri chili; cook 30 seconds. Add tomato and cook until thick and glossy, 4–5 minutes.
Brown chicken: Add marinated chicken with any yogurt. Cook over medium-high, stirring, until no longer pink on the outside, 4–5 minutes.
Simmer with spinach: Stir in spinach puree and 1/2 tsp salt. Reduce heat, cover, and simmer gently for 12–15 minutes until chicken reaches 165°F and is tender, stirring once or twice.
Finish and adjust: Uncover, simmer to desired thickness, 3–5 minutes. Stir in garam masala, black pepper, and lemon juice. Rest 2 minutes off heat.
Serve: Garnish with chopped cilantro and a drizzle of ghee if desired. Serve hot with basmati rice or roti.
tip: Sub 10 oz frozen spinach, thawed and well-squeezed. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; rewarm gently and finish with a squeeze of lemon to brighten.

title: General Tso's Chicken
ing: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 tbsp cornstarch, mixed with 2 tbsp water
1 tbsp scallions, thinly sliced, for garnish
steps: Pat chicken dry, season with 1/2 tsp kosher salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper. Whisk 1/2 cup cornstarch with 2 tbsp flour. Dip chicken in beaten eggs, then coat evenly in starch mixture.
In a bowl, whisk chicken broth, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, hoisin, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil, white pepper (optional), and the cornstarch slurry until smooth; set aside.
Heat a wok or deep skillet over medium-high to 350°F with frying oil. Fry coated chicken in batches until deep golden and cooked through to 165°F, about 4 to 5 minutes per batch. Drain on a rack.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp oil. Add dried chilies, stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant. Add garlic and ginger; stir-fry 20 seconds, taking care not to burn.
Whisk the sauce again, then pour into the wok. Bring to a lively simmer over medium-high and cook, stirring, until glossy and thick, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Return fried chicken to the wok and toss to coat evenly. Stir-fry 1 minute to re-crisp edges and fully glaze.
Plate immediately and garnish with scallions. Serve hot with steamed rice.
tip: For extra heat, add chili flakes with the dried chilies. Fry chicken once for tenderness or double-fry at 325°F then 375°F for extra crunch. Leftovers reheat well in a hot skillet in 5 minutes.

title: Orange Chicken
ing: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut 1-inch
1 tbsp cornstarch, mixed with 2 tbsp water
1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds, for garnish
2 tbsp scallions, thinly sliced, for garnish
steps: Marinate chicken with 2 tbsp soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil, salt, and pepper; toss and rest 10 minutes while you prep the sauce ingredients.
Whisk cornstarch, flour, and baking powder. Dip chicken in beaten eggs, then dredge in dry mix, pressing to coat; rest coated pieces 5 minutes to set.
Heat 1 inch frying oil in a deep skillet to 350°F. Fry chicken in batches 4 to 5 minutes until golden and 165°F internal; drain on a rack. Keep warm.
Pour off oil leaving 1 tbsp. Add ginger and garlic; stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant. Add orange zest, orange juice, sugar, rice vinegar, and 1 1/2 tbsp soy sauce; bring to a simmer 2 minutes.
Stir in red pepper flakes. Whisk in cornstarch slurry; simmer 1 to 2 minutes until glossy and thick enough to coat a spoon.
Add fried chicken to the pan; toss over medium heat 1 minute until evenly glazed. Adjust seasoning with salt, pepper, or vinegar to taste.
Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and scallions. Serve immediately with steamed rice.
tip: Sub thighs with breast if preferred; reduce fry time slightly. Sauce can be made 2 days ahead; reheat and thin with a splash of water before tossing with chicken.

title: Lemon Chicken
ing: 1 lb chicken thighs, boneless skinless, cut 1-inch
steps: Marinate chicken: In a bowl combine chicken, 1 tbsp soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil, salt, and white pepper. Mix, then add egg white and 1/2 cup cornstarch to coat. Chill 15 minutes.
Make lemon sauce: In a saucepan whisk sugar, chicken broth, lemon juice, lemon zest, rice vinegar, 1 tbsp soy sauce, and 1 tsp oil. Bring to a simmer over medium heat for 2 minutes.
Thicken sauce: Mix 1 tsp cornstarch with 2 tbsp water. Stir into simmering sauce and cook until glossy, 1–2 minutes. Keep warm on low.
Velvet batter: In a bowl whisk 1/3 cup cornstarch with 1/3 cup cold water to a smooth batter. Toss marinated chicken in batter to coat lightly.
Heat oil: In a wok or deep skillet, add frying oil to 1 1/2 inches and heat to 350°F. Line a rack over a sheet pan for draining.
Fry chicken: Fry chicken in batches at 340–350°F until golden and cooked through, 4–5 minutes, reaching 165°F internal. Drain on rack; let oil return to temp between batches.
Toss and serve: Place chicken in a clean bowl, pour over hot lemon sauce, and toss to coat evenly. Plate and garnish with lemon slices. Serve immediately with steamed rice.
tip: Substitute boneless breast for thigh if desired; reduce fry time slightly. Sauce keeps 3 days refrigerated; rewarm gently and re-crisp chicken in a 375°F oven for 8–10 minutes before saucing.

title: Sesame Chicken
ing: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut 1-inch
steps: Marinate chicken by tossing thighs with 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp pepper, 2 tbsp soy sauce, and 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine; rest 10 minutes while you prepare batter and sauce.
Make batter: whisk egg with 1/2 cup cornstarch, 1/2 cup flour, 1/2 tsp baking powder, and 1/2 cup cold water until just smooth; batter should ribbon and lightly coat chicken.
Stir sauce: combine 1/3 cup sugar, 1/4 cup soy sauce, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 2 tbsp ketchup, 2 tbsp toasted sesame oil, and 1/2 cup chicken broth; in a cup mix 2 tbsp cornstarch with 2 tbsp water.
Heat 1 1/2 to 2 inches frying oil in a deep pot to 350°F. Dip chicken in batter, letting excess drip. Fry in batches 4 to 5 minutes until pale golden and 165°F internal; drain on rack.
Increase oil to 375°F and refry chicken 1 to 2 minutes until deep golden and very crisp; drain well. Turn off heat.
In a large skillet, sauté garlic and ginger in 1 tbsp frying oil over medium heat for 30 seconds. Add sauce and bring to a boil; whisk in cornstarch slurry and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until glossy.
Add chicken to skillet and toss to coat evenly for 30 seconds. Sprinkle 2 tbsp toasted sesame seeds and toss again off heat.
Plate immediately and garnish with scallions to taste; serve hot with steamed rice.
tip: For a lighter coat, dust marinated chicken in cornstarch and shallow-fry. Sauce holds 4 days refrigerated; re-crisp chicken in a 400°F oven 8 minutes, then toss with reheated sauce.

title: Cashew Chicken
ing: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut 3/4-inch
steps: Toss chicken with 1 tbsp soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, 1 tsp cornstarch, and 1/4 tsp sugar; marinate 10 minutes while prepping vegetables and sauce.
Whisk sauce: 1 tbsp soy sauce, oyster sauce, hoisin, sesame oil, chicken broth, and 2 tsp cornstarch until smooth; set by the stove.
Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat 2 minutes. Add 1 tbsp oil. Stir-fry chicken in a single layer until browned and cooked to 165°F, about 4–5 minutes; transfer to a bowl.
Add 1 tbsp oil to wok. Stir-fry onion and bell pepper until crisp-tender, about 2 minutes. Add garlic and ginger; stir 20–30 seconds until fragrant.
Return chicken with any juices. Stir sauce, then pour in. Stir-fry until glossy and thickened, 1–2 minutes; if too thick, splash in 1–2 tbsp water.
Add cashews and scallions; toss 30 seconds. Season with white pepper and salt to taste. Remove from heat and serve immediately over steamed rice.
tip: Swap Shaoxing with dry sherry if needed. Keep cashews unsalted or reduce added salt. Leftovers keep 2 days refrigerated; reheat gently to preserve sauce gloss.

title: Three Cup Chicken
ing: 1 1/2 lb bone-in skin-on chicken thighs, chopped into 2-inch pieces
1/3 cup rice wine (Taiwanese mijiu or Shaoxing)
3 tbsp rock sugar, crushed (or 3 tbsp granulated sugar)
steps: Pat chicken dry. Heat 3 tbsp sesame oil in a 12-inch skillet or clay pot over medium-high until shimmering, 2 minutes. Add ginger and garlic; stir-fry until fragrant, 45 seconds.
Add chicken in a single layer; sear without moving until lightly browned, 3 minutes. Flip and brown the second side, 2–3 minutes.
Reduce heat to medium. Sprinkle in sugar; toss until it melts and lightly caramelizes on chicken, about 2 minutes.
Stir in soy sauce and rice wine. Bring to a lively simmer, then cover and cook over medium-low for 12 minutes, stirring once.
Uncover and raise heat to medium-high. Add scallions and chiles. Reduce sauce to a glossy, thick glaze that clings, 5–7 minutes, stirring frequently.
Drizzle in remaining 3 tbsp sesame oil. Add basil; toss until wilted and sauce is syrupy and bubbling, 30–60 seconds.
Check doneness: chicken should reach 165°F at the thickest part. Grind in black pepper to taste. Serve immediately with steamed rice.
tip: Use bone-in thighs for the best texture and gelatin; if using boneless, reduce covered simmer by 3–4 minutes. Leftovers keep 2 days chilled; rewarm gently to preserve the glaze.

title: White Cut Chicken
ing: 1 whole chicken (3.5 lb), room temp, excess fat trimmed
2 tbsp neutral frying oil, as needed
steps: Rinse and pat dry the chicken. Tie the legs together. Bring 10 cups water, 2 tbsp kosher salt, 4 slices ginger, 2 bruised scallions, and 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine to a rolling boil in a pot large enough to submerge the bird.
Lower heat to a bare simmer (about 190–195°F). Gently lower the chicken in, breast side down. Cover and poach for 12 minutes, maintaining just under a simmer—no vigorous bubbling.
Lift the chicken to drain, then return it to the pot breast side up. Cover and poach another 12 minutes. Repeat once more (total 36 minutes poaching), keeping liquid just shivering.
Turn off heat, cover, and let the chicken steep in the hot broth for 20 minutes, until the thickest thigh reads 165°F and juices run clear. Prepare a large ice bath with 4 cups ice and cold water.
Transfer chicken to the ice bath for 8 minutes to firm skin, then drain well. Pat dry. Rub skin lightly with a few drops of sesame oil if desired. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.

For ginger-scallion oil, heat 2 tbsp neutral frying oil until shimmering. In a heatproof bowl, combine 4 minced scallions, 2 tbsp minced ginger, and 1 tsp kosher salt. Pour hot oil over, then stir in 1/4 cup hot poaching broth and 1 tsp sesame oil.
Make dipping sauce by mixing 1 tbsp light soy sauce, 2 tbsp hot poaching broth, and 1 tsp sugar. Taste and adjust salt to taste.
To serve, chop chicken Chinese-style through the bone into bite-size pieces or carve off the bone. Arrange over sliced cucumber. Serve warm or room temp with ginger-scallion oil and soy-broth dip.
tip: Save extra poaching broth for congee or soup. For a larger bird, add 3–5 minutes poaching and 5 minutes steeping; always confirm 165°F at the thigh close to the bone.

title: Chicken Chow Mein
ing: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, thinly sliced
1 cup bean sprouts, rinsed and drained
1/2 cup celery, thinly sliced on the bias
steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Cook chow mein noodles until just shy of tender, 2 to 3 minutes. Drain, rinse briefly under cold water, and shake dry; toss with 1 tsp frying oil.
In a bowl, combine chicken, 1 tbsp soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, cornstarch, and sesame oil; mix to coat and marinate 10 minutes.
Make the sauce: whisk oyster sauce, remaining 1 tbsp soy sauce, dark soy sauce, sugar, white pepper, and chicken broth; set aside.
Heat a 12-inch wok or skillet over high until smoking. Add 1 tbsp frying oil. Stir-fry chicken in a single layer until browned and cooked through, 4 to 5 minutes; remove.
Add 1 tbsp frying oil, then garlic, ginger, and onion; stir-fry 30 seconds. Add cabbage, celery, and carrots; stir-fry until crisp-tender, 2 minutes.
Add noodles and bean sprouts; stir-fry, tossing to heat through, 1 to 2 minutes. Return chicken and add scallions.
Pour in sauce; stir-fry until noodles are evenly coated and glossy and sauce reduces, 1 to 2 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, hot. If desired, drizzle a few drops of sesame oil to finish.
tip: Swap thighs for breast if preferred; slice thin and cook just to doneness. Leftovers keep 2 days chilled; reheat in a hot skillet with a splash of water to revive noodles.

title: Chicken Teriyaki
ing: 1 tsp sesame seeds, for garnish, optional
2 tbsp scallions, thinly sliced, for garnish, optional
steps: Stir soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar in a bowl until sugar dissolves; reserve 2 tbsp separately for finishing glaze.
Pat chicken dry and lightly season with black pepper. Warm a large skillet over medium heat and add a thin film of frying oil.
Place chicken skin side down and cook without moving until skin is deep golden and crisp, about 7–8 minutes. Spoon off excess fat as needed.
Flip chicken and cook until juices run clear and internal temperature reaches 165°F, about 5–6 minutes more.
Pour the larger portion of sauce into the skillet. Simmer, turning chicken, until bubbling vigorously and reduced, about 2–3 minutes.
Whisk water and cornstarch, then stir into skillet. Add reserved 2 tbsp sauce and simmer until glossy and syrupy, 1–2 minutes.
Transfer chicken to a board, rest 2 minutes, then slice into bite-size strips. Return slices to skillet and toss to coat, 30 seconds.
Plate chicken over rice if desired, spooning sauce over. Garnish with sesame seeds and scallions.
tip: Skin-on thighs give classic lacquer and flavor; substitute boneless skinless if needed. Leftovers keep 2 days refrigerated; rewarm gently to avoid breaking the glaze.

title: Chicken Katsu
steps: Pat chicken dry, season both sides with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper, and let stand 5 minutes while you set up breading.
Set up three bowls: flour in one; beaten eggs in the second; panko in the third. Dredge chicken in flour, shake off excess.
Dip floured chicken in egg to coat, then press firmly into panko on both sides until evenly covered. Rest breaded cutlets 5 minutes.
Heat 1/2 inch frying oil in a large skillet to 350°F over medium heat. Maintain 325–350°F during frying.
Fry 1–2 cutlets at a time until deeply golden, 3–4 minutes per side; turn once. Cook to an internal temperature of 165°F. Drain on a rack.
While cutlets rest 3 minutes, mound shredded cabbage on plates and portion hot rice alongside.
Slice katsu crosswise into 3/4-inch strips. Arrange over rice or beside cabbage.
Drizzle or serve with tonkatsu sauce and lemon wedges for squeezing at the table.
tip: Sub pork loin for a classic tonkatsu. Keep fried cutlets crisp on a 200°F rack up to 20 minutes. Leftovers re-crisp in a 375°F oven for 8–10 min; avoid microwaving.

title: Yakitori
ing: 1 lb boneless skin-on chicken thighs, trimmed
4 stalks Japanese negi or 6 scallions, cut into 1-inch pieces
steps: Soak bamboo skewers in cold water for 30 minutes to prevent burning. Trim excess fat from chicken, then cut chicken into 1-inch bite-size squares, keeping skin attached where possible.

Make tare: In a small saucepan combine soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, and rice vinegar. Bring to a gentle boil over medium heat, then simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until glossy and reduced to a light syrup. Set aside.
Thread skewers: Alternate chicken pieces and negi/scallion segments on soaked skewers, packing snugly to promote even cooking. Lightly brush with frying oil and season lightly with salt and pepper.
Preheat a grill to medium-high (about 425°F). Clean and oil grates. Place skewers over direct heat and sear, turning every 1 to 2 minutes, until lightly charred, about 6 to 8 minutes total.
Brush skewers generously with tare, then continue grilling 2 to 4 minutes, turning and basting often, until chicken reaches 165°F at the thickest piece and glaze is lacquered.
Transfer to a platter and brush once more with tare. Rest 2 minutes to set the glaze, then serve immediately with extra tare on the side.
tip: Use skin-on thighs for authentic texture and basting fat. Leftover tare keeps 1 week refrigerated; boil 1 minute before reusing as sauce or glaze.

title: Oyakodon
ing: 1 1/2 lb boneless skin-on chicken thighs, trimmed and cut into 3/4-inch pieces
4 cups cooked Japanese short-grain rice, hot
2 tbsp scallions, thinly sliced, for garnish
1 tbsp neutral frying oil, as needed
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Add sliced onions and cook until translucent and tender, 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in dashi, soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat and cook 2 minutes to meld flavors.
Add chicken in an even layer. Simmer gently, uncovered, turning once, until just cooked through to 165°F, 6 to 8 minutes.
Reduce heat to low. Pour half of the beaten eggs evenly over the chicken and onions. Cover and cook until softly set, about 45 to 60 seconds.
Gently swirl the pan. Pour in remaining eggs, cover, and steam on low until custardy with a slight wobble, 45 to 60 seconds more. Do not overcook.
Spoon hot rice into 4 bowls, about 1 cup each. Slide a quarter of the chicken-egg mixture over each bowl, including some broth.
Garnish with scallions and serve immediately while hot and silky.
tip: For a milder sweetness, reduce sugar to 1 tbsp. Leftovers keep 1 day; reheat gently to avoid overcooking the eggs.

title: Korean Fried Chicken
ing: 2 lb chicken wings, flats and drumettes separated
2 tbsp roasted peanuts, chopped, for garnish
2 tbsp scallions, thinly sliced, for garnish
1 tsp toasted sesame seeds, for garnish
steps: Pat chicken dry, toss with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper, and let stand at room temperature for 15 minutes to season.
In a shallow bowl, whisk eggs. In another, mix potato starch and flour. Dip chicken in egg, then dredge in starch mixture, pressing to coat; rest on a rack 10 minutes.
For yangnyeom sauce, simmer gochujang, ketchup, brown sugar, soy sauce, rice syrup, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger, and sesame oil over low heat for 3 to 4 minutes, then keep warm.
Heat frying oil to 320°F in a heavy pot (2 inches deep). Fry chicken in batches 6 to 7 minutes until pale and set; drain on a rack. Let oil return to 320°F between batches.
Increase oil to 375°F. Double-fry chicken 2 to 3 minutes per batch until deep golden and ultra-crisp; internal temperature must reach 165°F. Drain on a rack 2 minutes.
Toss half the chicken with warm yangnyeom sauce until glossy. Leave the remaining half plain for soy-garlic style (or keep plain if you prefer extra-crispy).
Optional soy-garlic glaze: In a small pan simmer 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp water, 1 tsp minced garlic for 2 minutes; drizzle over the plain half and toss quickly.
Plate immediately; garnish with peanuts, scallions, and sesame seeds. Serve hot with pickled radish on the side.
tip: Potato starch is key for shatter-crisp crust; cornstarch works in a pinch. Double-fried chicken stays crisp; reheat at 375°F for 8 minutes on a rack to refresh.

title: Dak Galbi
ing: 1.5 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut 1-inch
1 cup sweet potato, peeled and 1/4-inch slices
1 cup rice cakes (tteok), soaked 10 minutes if hard
1 tsp toasted sesame oil, for garnish
steps: Make marinade: in a bowl mix gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, rice syrup, mirin, garlic, and ginger until smooth, 2 minutes.
Marinate chicken: add chicken to marinade, coat well, cover, and refrigerate for 20 to 30 minutes while you prep vegetables and soak rice cakes.
Heat a large cast-iron or nonstick skillet over medium-high, add 1 tbsp oil. Spread marinated chicken in an even layer and cook 3 minutes undisturbed.
Add cabbage and sweet potato, toss, then add rice cakes and mushrooms. Cook, stirring and pressing to sear, 8 to 10 minutes until chicken is browned and vegetables begin to soften.
Reduce to medium, cover, and cook 5 to 7 minutes until sweet potato is tender and chicken reaches 165°F internal temperature. Add a splash of water if pan looks dry.
Stir in scallions and perilla leaves, cook 1 to 2 minutes until just wilted. Adjust seasoning with salt and black pepper to taste.
Drizzle sesame oil, sprinkle sesame seeds, and serve sizzling straight from the pan with steamed rice and lettuce wraps if desired.
tip: Soak refrigerated tteok in warm water 10 minutes to soften. For more Chuncheon-style bite, add 1/2 cup cabbage more and 1/2 cup thin-sliced carrot or use young perilla if available.

title: Hainanese Chicken Rice
ing: 1 cup jasmine rice, rinsed until water runs clear
2 tbsp chicken fat or frying oil, as needed
1 bunch cilantro, for garnish, as needed
steps: Rub chicken skin with 2 tbsp kosher salt to exfoliate, then rinse and pat dry. Stuff cavity with 2 oz ginger slices, 4 cloves crushed garlic, and 2 scallion stalks; tie legs loosely with kitchen twine.
Bring 8 cups water to a boil in a pot large enough to submerge chicken. Lower to a bare simmer (about 190°F). Gently lower chicken in, breast side down; maintain a gentle tremble, not a boil.
Poach for 35–40 minutes to 165°F in the thickest breast. Lift chicken, drain cavity, and plunge into an ice bath for 5 minutes to tighten skin. Reserve broth; skim and keep hot.
For rice, render 2 tbsp chicken fat or heat frying oil over medium. Sauté minced garlic and minced ginger for 1 minute until fragrant. Add rinsed rice; stir to coat and turn glossy, 2 minutes.
Stir in 1 1/2 cups hot reserved broth and 1/2 tsp salt. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce to low, and steam for 15 minutes. Off heat, rest 10 minutes, then fluff.
Whisk 4 tbsp light soy sauce, 2 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tbsp sugar, and 1/2 cup hot broth to make serving sauce. Season broth with white pepper to taste for soup; keep hot.
Remove twine. Carve chicken Chinese-style: separate legs and wings, slice breast on the bone, then debone into neat slices. Toss pieces lightly with some serving sauce to gloss.

Plate rice with sliced chicken, ladle a small bowl of hot broth on the side. Garnish with cucumber slices and cilantro. Serve remaining sauce alongside; add chili and ginger-scallion sauces if desired.
tip: Save extra broth for soup noodles; it freezes well. Traditional condiments: chili-garlic sauce and ginger-scallion relish—make ahead and refrigerate up to 1 week.

title: Chicken Satay
ing: 1 1/2 lb chicken thighs, trimmed and 1-inch cubed
10 oz roasted unsalted peanuts, finely ground
1 tbsp roasted peanuts, chopped, for garnish
steps: Soak 12 wooden skewers in water for 20 minutes. In a bowl, whisk 1/3 cup kecap manis, 2 tbsp lime juice, 2 tbsp palm sugar, 3 tbsp coconut milk, garlic, ginger, coriander, turmeric, salt, and pepper.
Add chicken to the marinade, toss to coat, and chill for 20 minutes while you make the sauce. Thread marinated chicken tightly onto soaked skewers.

Make peanut sauce: In a saucepan, combine ground peanuts, 1 1/2 cups hot water, 2 tbsp tamarind paste, 1 tbsp kecap manis, and 1 tbsp palm sugar. Simmer over medium-low, stirring, for 8–10 minutes until thick and glossy.
Adjust sauce with a splash of water for dipping consistency; keep warm over low. Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high (about 425°F). Brush grates lightly with frying oil.
Grill skewers 3–4 minutes per side, basting lightly with a little kecap manis in the last minute. Cook until chicken reaches 165°F at the center, 8–10 minutes total.
Rest skewers 3 minutes. If desired, briefly warm a few spoonfuls of sauce on the grill to pick up smoke, stirring back into the pot.
Serve skewers with warm peanut sauce, chopped roasted peanuts, cilantro, and lime wedges. Spoon a little sauce over and squeeze lime just before eating.
tip: Substitute brown sugar for palm sugar if needed. Peanut sauce keeps 4 days refrigerated; loosen with hot water when reheating. Serve with steamed rice cakes (lontong) for extra authenticity.

title: Ayam Goreng
ing: 2 lb bone-in chicken pieces, skin-on, cut into 8 pieces
1 cup fresh basil leaves, optional garnish
steps: Combine garlic, shallots, ginger, galangal, coriander, turmeric, palm sugar, salt, and pepper into a paste using a mortar or processor, about 2 minutes.
Rub paste all over chicken; add lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves. Pour in coconut water and rice vinegar, toss to coat, and marinate 30 minutes.
Transfer everything to a pot. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, cover, and cook for 20 minutes, turning once, until chicken reaches 165°F.
Uncover and simmer for 5 to 8 minutes to reduce until most liquid evaporates and seasonings cling to chicken. Remove lemongrass and lime leaves; cool 10 minutes.
Heat frying oil in a wok or deep skillet to 350°F. Fry chicken in batches 4 to 6 minutes, turning, until deep golden and skin crisp; internal temp 175°F for thighs/drumsticks.
Drain on a rack 3 minutes. Fry the leftover aromatics from the pot 30 to 45 seconds at 350°F until crisp; drain.
Serve chicken hot with the crisped aromatics and basil leaves. Accompany with steamed rice and sambal, if desired.
tip: Palm sugar can be swapped with light brown sugar. Par-cooked chicken can be cooled and refrigerated up to 24 hours; fry just before serving for best crispness.

title: Ayam Penyet
ing: 2 lb chicken leg quarters, separated into thighs and drumsticks
14 oz firm tofu, cut into 8 slabs
8 oz small cucumbers, cut into batons
steps: Simmer chicken with water, coconut water, salt, sugar, garlic, shallots, galangal, ginger, kaffir lime leaves, lemongrass, and tamarind over medium heat for 25–30 minutes until 165°F at the bone; let drain 10 minutes.
Pat chicken dry. Heat frying oil to 350°F in a deep skillet. Fry chicken in batches 5–7 minutes until deep golden and 175°F at thickest; rest 5 minutes on a rack.
Fry tofu and tempeh in the same oil at 350°F for 3–4 minutes until crisp and golden; drain. Reserve some crisp crumbs in the pan for serving.
For sambal: in 2 tbsp reserved oil, sauté chilies, garlic, shallots, and tomatoes over medium heat for 6–8 minutes until soft and lightly charred.
Pound sautéed mixture with shrimp paste and palm sugar in a mortar (or pulse) to a coarse paste; season with salt and lime juice. Keep warm.
Lightly smash each fried chicken piece with a pestle or the flat of a cleaver to crack the surface without breaking apart.
Spread warm sambal on a serving plate. Press chicken onto sambal to coat the underside; top with tofu, tempeh, and a sprinkle of reserved crisp crumbs.
Serve immediately with cucumbers, Thai basil, and steamed rice on the side.
tip: Sub bird’s eye chilies for more heat. Keep sambal up to 3 days refrigerated; rewarm with a little oil before serving. For airier crumbs, dust tofu/tempeh lightly with rice flour before frying.

title: Chicken Rendang
ing: 2 lb bone-in chicken thighs, skin-on, cut into large chunks
3 tbsp neutral frying oil, as needed
8 oz fresh grated coconut (kerisik), toasted until deep golden
3 stalks lemongrass, white parts only, bruised
1 1/2 tsp fine sea salt, to taste
steps: Make the spice paste: blend soaked dried chilies, fresh chilies, shallots, garlic, galangal, ginger, and turmeric with 2 tbsp oil and a splash of water until very smooth.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a Dutch oven over medium. Fry the spice paste and bruised lemongrass, stirring, until thick, aromatic, and the oil splits, about 10–12 minutes.
Add chicken and turn to coat, cooking until no longer pink on the outside, about 4–5 minutes. Stir in coconut milk and water; bring to a gentle simmer.
Add kaffir lime leaves, salt, and palm sugar. Reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered, stirring every 5–7 minutes, until sauce is reduced and glossy, about 45 minutes.
Stir in toasted grated coconut (kerisik). Continue to cook on low, stirring frequently, until the gravy turns dark, thick, and clings to the chicken, 20–30 minutes.
Adjust seasoning with salt and white pepper to taste. Continue cooking until chicken is very tender and sauce is almost dry, 5–10 minutes more.
For food safety, ensure chicken reaches 165°F at the thickest part. Rest 5 minutes off heat before serving.
tip: Make kerisik by toasting grated coconut in a dry pan, 10–15 min, stirring. Rendang improves overnight; cool, refrigerate up to 3 days, reheat gently with a splash of water.

title: Chicken Laksa
ing: 1 lb chicken thighs, boneless skinless, sliced 1/2-inch
1 tsp kosher salt, or to taste
1/2 cup laksa leaves (Vietnamese coriander/daun kesum), chopped, for garnish
1 cup laksa paste, homemade or good-quality store-bought
steps: Soak 8 oz rice vermicelli in hot water until pliable, 6 to 8 minutes, then drain. Blanch in boiling water for 30 seconds just before serving to heat through.
Heat 2 tbsp frying oil over medium heat. Add 1 cup laksa paste and fry, stirring, until aromatic and the oil splits, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add 1 lb sliced chicken thighs and cook, stirring, until opaque on the outside, 3 minutes. Pour in 4 cups chicken stock and bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer for 8 minutes.
Stir in 1 cup coconut milk, 1 tbsp palm sugar, 1 tsp salt, and 1 tbsp fish sauce. Simmer gently for 5 minutes; do not boil hard to prevent splitting. Chicken should reach 165°F.
Add 4 oz tofu puffs and warm through, 2 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt or fish sauce as needed.
Blanch the soaked noodles for 30 seconds, then divide among 4 warmed bowls. Add a handful of bean sprouts to each bowl.
Ladle hot laksa broth and chicken over noodles, ensuring some tofu puffs in each bowl. Rest 1 minute to soften sprouts slightly.
Finish with 2 tbsp lime juice to the pot or to taste at the table. Serve with sambal oelek and scatter laksa leaves and cilantro generously over each bowl.
tip: Daun kesum is traditional; if unavailable, use a mix of cilantro and mint. Laksa paste varies—add more stock if too thick or more paste for heat. Broth keeps 2 days refrigerated; reheat gently.

title: Thai Basil Chicken (Pad Krapow Gai)
ing: 2 tbsp neutral frying oil, as needed
4 Thai bird’s eye chilies, finely chopped
1 cup long beans or green beans, sliced 1/2-inch
2 cups Thai holy basil leaves, loosely packed
4 large eggs, as needed for frying
steps: Prep sauces: In a small bowl mix oyster sauce, light soy, dark soy, fish sauce, and sugar until dissolved; set aside.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large wok over high heat until shimmering, about 1 minute. Add garlic and chilies; stir-fry 20–30 seconds until fragrant, avoiding browning.
Add ground chicken and spread in an even layer. Stir-fry over high heat until no pink remains and small browned bits form, 4–5 minutes; break up clumps. Chicken should reach 165°F.
Add onion and beans; stir-fry 2 minutes. Splash in chicken broth and the mixed sauces; stir-fry until beans are crisp-tender and liquid is mostly reduced, 2–3 minutes.
Turn off heat. Add Thai holy basil and white pepper; toss just until basil wilts and releases aroma, 15–20 seconds. Taste and adjust fish sauce or sugar if needed.

In a separate skillet, heat 1–2 tbsp oil over medium-high. Crack in eggs and fry until edges lace and yolks are set to preference, 2–3 minutes for runny. Season lightly with a pinch of salt if desired.
Serve immediately over hot jasmine rice, topping each portion with a crispy fried egg and spooning extra pan sauce over rice.
tip: Holy basil is traditional; if unavailable, use Thai basil. Stir-fry fast over high heat to keep basil bright. Leftovers keep 2 days refrigerated; reheat quickly to avoid overcooking.

title: Khao Man Gai
steps: Rinse chicken and place in a pot with 8 cups water and 1 tbsp kosher salt. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then lower to barely bubbling and poach for 35–40 minutes until tender and 165°F at the thickest part.

Transfer chicken to a plate to rest 10 minutes; strain and reserve the broth. When cool enough, debone and slice chicken, keeping skin on. Skim 2 tbsp chicken fat from the broth for the rice (or render from skin).
Heat 2 tbsp chicken fat in a pot over medium heat. Add 2 tbsp minced garlic and sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in rinsed jasmine rice to coat for 1 minute until glossy.
Add 1 1/4 cups warm chicken broth to the rice, bring to a gentle boil, then cover, reduce heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from heat and steam covered for 10 minutes more.

Make the nam jim: In a bowl combine mashed fermented soybeans, dark soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, finely minced ginger, finely minced garlic, and chopped Thai chilies. Stir until sugar dissolves; adjust to taste.
Warm 2 cups reserved broth. Season lightly with salt to taste. Keep hot for serving as sipping broth or to moisten rice.
To serve, mound garlicky rice on each plate, top with sliced chicken, and spoon some sauce over or serve on the side. Garnish with cucumber slices and chopped cilantro.
Ladle hot broth into small bowls alongside. Serve immediately so rice stays fluffy and chicken skin supple.
tip: Tao jiew is key; if unavailable, mix 3 tbsp light soy with 1 tbsp miso. Refrigerate sauce up to 1 week; rewarm broth before serving. For extra aroma, add 3 slices ginger to the poaching liquid.

title: Gai Yang (Thai Grilled Chicken)
ing: 3 lb bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks
1 tbsp cilantro roots or stems, minced
1 tbsp fresh cilantro, chopped, for garnish
steps: Pound garlic, cilantro roots, white pepper, coriander, and turmeric to a fine paste. In a bowl whisk paste with coconut milk, fish sauce, soy sauce, and palm sugar until dissolved.
Pat chicken dry, score thickest parts, and coat evenly with marinade. Cover and refrigerate for 45 to 60 minutes (up to 12 hours for deeper flavor).
Heat grill to medium (375–400°F). Oil grates lightly. Remove excess marinade from chicken and let stand at room temp 10 minutes.
Grill chicken skin-side down over direct heat 5 to 7 minutes until well marked; move to indirect heat, cover, and cook at 375–400°F for 25 to 35 minutes, turning once.
Baste with any reserved marinade during the last 10 minutes. Cook until juices run clear and internal temperature reaches 165°F in the thickest part.
Rest chicken on a platter for 5 to 10 minutes. Season lightly with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot with lime wedges and chopped cilantro garnish.
tip: Substitute light brown sugar for palm sugar if needed. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; rewarm gently or eat at room temp. For smokier flavor, add a small handful of soaked hardwood chips to the coals.

title: Chicken Panang Curry
ing: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, thinly sliced
6 kaffir lime leaves, 3 finely sliced, 3 torn
1 cup red bell pepper, thin strips
1/2 cup Thai basil leaves, loosely packed
steps: Chill 1/2 cup coconut milk until very cold, then open the can without shaking. Skim 1/2 cup thick cream from the top and set aside; reserve remaining coconut milk separately.
Warm 1 tsp peanut oil in a wide saucepan over medium heat. Add the reserved thick coconut cream and cook, stirring, until it splits and the oil surfaces, about 3 to 5 minutes.
Stir in 3 tbsp Panang curry paste and fry in the coconut oil, stirring constantly, until fragrant and glossy, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add sliced chicken thighs and toss to coat in the paste. Cook until the exterior turns opaque, 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour in remaining coconut milk and 1 cup chicken broth. Add torn kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Season with 2 tsp palm sugar and 1 tbsp fish sauce. Add red bell pepper strips and simmer until chicken reaches 165°F and peppers are tender-crisp, 5 to 7 minutes.
Stir in sliced kaffir lime leaves and most of the Thai basil. Simmer 1 minute, then taste and adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Rest off heat 2 minutes to settle. Garnish with remaining basil and serve hot over steamed jasmine rice.
tip: Kaffir lime leaves are essential; if unavailable, use 1 tsp very fine lime zest. Curry thickens as it rests; thin with warm broth as needed.

title: Chicken Adobo
ing: 1/2 tsp ground black pepper, to taste
1 cup cooked jasmine rice, for serving, as needed
2 tbsp scallions, thinly sliced, for garnish, as needed
steps: Pat chicken dry. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide pot over medium-high until shimmering. Brown chicken skin-side down until deep golden, 6–8 minutes; flip and brown 3 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp fat. Add smashed garlic and cook until fragrant, 30 seconds. Stir in soy sauce, cane vinegar, water, brown sugar, peppercorns, and bay leaves; scrape up browned bits.
Return chicken skin-side up. Bring to a boil over medium-high, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cover and cook for 20 minutes.
Uncover, flip chicken, and simmer uncovered until tender and sauce reduces slightly, 10–12 minutes.
Flip chicken skin-side up. Increase heat to medium-high and simmer to glaze and thicken the sauce to a syrupy consistency, 5–7 minutes. Skim excess fat. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Check doneness: chicken should reach 165°F at the thickest part. Remove bay leaves.
Serve chicken and spoon glossy adobo sauce over hot jasmine rice. Garnish with sliced scallions if desired.
tip: Cane vinegar yields the classic tang; substitute rice vinegar if needed. Chill up to 4 days; flavors deepen. Reheat gently, adding a splash of water if sauce is too tight.

title: Chicken Tinola
ing: 2 lb bone-in chicken pieces, cut into serving pieces
2 oz fresh ginger, peeled and thinly sliced
2 cups green papaya, peeled and cut into 1-inch wedges
2 cups water spinach leaves (or spinach), roughly torn
1/2 tsp ground black pepper, to taste
2 long green chilies (siling pansigang), slit lengthwise
steps: Pat chicken dry and season lightly with salt. Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pot over medium; brown chicken pieces 3 to 4 minutes per side to render fat and add flavor.
Add onion, garlic, and ginger; sauté until onion is translucent and ginger fragrant, about 3 minutes, scraping browned bits.
Pour in 6 cups chicken broth and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 20 minutes until chicken is cooked through to 165°F.
Stir in fish sauce and pepper. Taste and adjust salt to balance salinity and ginger heat.
Add green papaya wedges and slit green chilies; simmer uncovered until papaya is just tender but not mushy, 10 to 12 minutes.
Skim excess fat. Turn off heat and stir in water spinach leaves until just wilted, about 30 seconds.
Ladle hot tinola into bowls, ensuring a mix of broth, chicken, papaya, and greens. Serve immediately with steamed rice.
tip: Sub green papaya with chayote if unavailable. Cool leftovers quickly and refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat gently without boiling to keep greens vibrant.

title: Chicken Inasal
ing: 2 lb bone-in chicken thighs, skin-on, scored
1 lime, cut into wedges, for serving
steps: Whisk cane vinegar, calamansi juice, lemon-lime soda, garlic, ginger, brown sugar, salt, pepper, soy sauce, and lemongrass. Reserve 1/4 cup for basting. Pour remaining over chicken and marinate 45 minutes at room temp.
Meanwhile, combine warm annatto oil with melted butter and 2 tbsp reserved marinade to make basting sauce; set aside. Lightly oil grill grates with frying oil.
Preheat a charcoal or gas grill to medium heat (375–400°F). Drain chicken well; pat dry to encourage browning.
Grill chicken skin side down over direct heat 6–8 minutes until lightly charred, moving to avoid flare-ups. Flip and grill 6 minutes more, basting with annatto-butter every 2–3 minutes.
Move chicken to indirect heat, cover, and cook 15–20 minutes, basting twice, until juices run clear and internal temp reaches 165°F at thickest part.
Finish skin side down over direct heat 1–2 minutes for crisping; baste once more and rest 5 minutes on a platter.
Warm any remaining basting sauce to a brief simmer for 1 minute and spoon over rested chicken.
Serve hot with lime wedges and steamed rice; spoon drippings over rice if desired.
tip: Cane vinegar gives classic tang; substitute white vinegar if needed. Marinate up to 4 hours chilled; bring to room temp 20 minutes before grilling for even cooking.

title: Phở Gà (Vietnamese Chicken Noodle Soup)
ing: 1 tbsp fish sauce, plus more to taste
12 oz dried flat rice noodles (bánh phở)
1 cup cilantro and Thai basil, roughly chopped
steps: Char aromatics: Place onion halves and ginger slices cut-side down in a dry skillet over medium-high heat until deeply charred, 6 to 8 minutes; set aside and rinse off loose soot.
Parboil chicken: Add chicken to a large pot, cover with 4 qt cold water, bring to a rolling boil over high heat, boil 2 minutes, then drain and rinse chicken and pot to remove scum.

Simmer broth: Refill pot with 4 qt water, add chicken, charred onion and ginger. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat and skim. Partially cover and simmer for 35 to 40 minutes until chicken reaches 165°F at the thigh.
Toast spices: While broth simmers, toast coriander, fennel, cloves, star anise, and cinnamon in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant, 2 minutes. Tie in cheesecloth or a tea infuser.

Finish broth: Remove chicken to cool. Add spice bundle, rock sugar, 1 tbsp fish sauce, and 1 tsp salt to the pot; simmer gently for 30 minutes, then discard aromatics and spices. Season with fish sauce, salt, and pepper to taste.
Shred chicken: When cool enough, pull meat from bones and shred or slice; reserve skin if desired. Strain broth through a fine sieve for clarity and keep at a bare simmer.

Prepare noodles and toppings: Soak dried rice noodles in hot tap water until pliable, 20 to 30 minutes. Blanch in boiling water until tender, 30 to 60 seconds; drain. Arrange sliced onion, scallions, herbs, sprouts, lime, and jalapeño.
Assemble: Divide noodles among 4 bowls, top with chicken and a few onion slices. Ladle boiling broth over to warm through. Serve with herbs, sprouts, lime, jalapeño, and extra fish sauce.
tip: For clearer broth, cool and skim fat, then reheat. Sub poached bone-in chicken thighs (2.5 lb) for the whole bird; simmer thighs 25 to 30 minutes to 175°F, then proceed.

title: Vietnamese Lemongrass Chicken
ing: 1 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 lime, cut into wedges, for garnish
steps: In a bowl, combine chicken, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp brown sugar, black pepper, and lime juice; toss to coat and marinate for 15 minutes while you prep aromatics.
In a separate small bowl, mix remaining 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp brown sugar, and 1/3 cup water to make a sauce; set aside.
Heat 1 tbsp frying oil in a large skillet over medium-high until shimmering, about 1 minute. Add lemongrass and shallot; stir-fry until fragrant, 1 to 2 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, and chilies; stir-fry 30 seconds. Push aromatics to the edges, add 1 tbsp oil if needed, then add chicken in a single layer; sear without moving for 2 minutes.
Stir-fry chicken until lightly browned on all sides, 3 to 4 minutes. Pour in the sauce and bring to a lively simmer over medium-high heat.
Simmer, stirring occasionally, until chicken is cooked through to 165°F and liquids reduce to a glossy coating, 4 to 6 minutes. Season with salt to taste.
Turn off heat and fold in scallions. Rest 1 minute to let flavors settle.
Transfer to a platter, garnish with cilantro and lime wedges, and serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.
tip: Use only the pale, tender inner stalks of lemongrass; bruise before mincing for best aroma. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; rewarm gently with a splash of water to loosen the sauce.

title: Classic Roast Turkey
ing: 1 8- to 10-lb turkey, thawed and giblets removed
1 cup low-sodium turkey or chicken broth
steps: Pat turkey dry thoroughly with paper towels and let stand at room temperature for 45 minutes to take the chill off.
Adjust oven rack to lower-middle and heat oven to 425°F. Rub skin with 2 tbsp softened butter and oil; season outside and cavity with salt and pepper.
Stuff cavity loosely with onion, lemon, and thyme. Tuck wing tips under, tie legs loosely with kitchen twine for even roasting.
Place turkey breast-side up on a rack set in a roasting pan; pour 1 cup broth into the pan to prevent drips from burning.
Roast at 425°F for 30 minutes to set the skin, then reduce oven to 325°F. Tent breast lightly with foil if browning too quickly.
Continue roasting at 325°F, basting pan juices every 30 minutes, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest thigh reads 165°F, about 1¾ to 2¼ hours total.
Transfer turkey to a carving board, tent with foil, and rest for 25 to 30 minutes so juices redistribute.
Meanwhile, skim fat from pan drippings for gravy if desired. Carve turkey, discarding stuffing aromatics, and serve warm.
tip: For herb butter, mash 2 tbsp chopped parsley and 1 tsp minced thyme into the butter. Leftovers keep 3 to 4 days refrigerated; reheat covered with a splash of broth to keep moist.

title: Turkey Burgers
steps: In a bowl, gently mix ground turkey, breadcrumbs, grated onion, Worcestershire, Dijon, garlic powder, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper until just combined; do not overwork.
Divide mixture into 4 equal portions and form 3/4-inch-thick patties with a slight center dimple to prevent doming.
Heat a large skillet or grill to medium-high (about 400°F). Lightly oil the surface and place patties dimple-side up.
Cook 4–5 minutes until well browned. Flip and cook 4–6 minutes more until an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 165°F.
Top each patty with cheese during the last 1 minute of cooking to melt. Transfer patties to a plate and rest 3 minutes.
Toast buns until golden, about 1–2 minutes. Stir mayonnaise until spreadable and season with a pinch of pepper to taste.
Assemble burgers: spread mayonnaise on buns, add lettuce and tomato, then the turkey patty. Cap with top bun and serve immediately.
tip: Swap cheddar with Swiss or pepper jack. Cooked patties keep 3 days refrigerated; reheat to 165°F. Add 1–2 tbsp milk if the mix feels dry.

title: Turkey Chili
ing: 14.5 oz canned diced tomatoes, with juices
15 oz canned kidney beans, drained and rinsed
steps: Warm 1 tbsp oil in a heavy pot over medium heat until shimmering, 2 minutes.
Add onion and bell pepper; cook, stirring, until softened and lightly golden, 6 to 8 minutes. Stir in garlic; cook 30 seconds.
Push vegetables to sides; add ground turkey. Cook, breaking up, until no longer pink and crumbled, 5 to 6 minutes; internal temp should reach 165°F.
Stir in chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, oregano, and cayenne; cook until fragrant, 30 seconds. Add tomato paste; cook, stirring, 1 minute.
Pour in diced tomatoes and chicken broth; bring to a boil over medium-high heat, 2 to 3 minutes.
Reduce to a gentle simmer, uncovered, and cook, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened and flavors meld, 25 to 30 minutes.
Stir in kidney beans; simmer for 5 minutes more. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Rest off heat 5 minutes. Ladle into warm bowls and serve hot.
tip: Swap kidney beans with pinto beans if preferred. Chili keeps 4 days refrigerated; flavor improves overnight. Reheat gently with a splash of broth if thick.

title: Turkey Meatballs
ing: 1 tbsp olive oil, for frying as needed
1 tbsp chopped parsley, for garnish as needed
steps: In a bowl, combine breadcrumbs and milk; let stand for 5 minutes to hydrate.
Add ground turkey, egg, Parmesan, parsley, garlic, onion powder, salt, and pepper; mix gently until just combined.
With damp hands, form 16 golf-ball-size meatballs (about 1.5 oz each), rolling lightly to avoid compacting.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat until shimmering, then brown meatballs on 2–3 sides, 5–6 minutes total; do not cook through.
Drain excess fat if needed. Add marinara and 1/2 cup water; stir gently to nestle meatballs. Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Cover and simmer gently for 12–15 minutes until meatballs reach 165°F in the center; spoon sauce over them occasionally.
Uncover and simmer 3–5 minutes to thicken sauce to desired consistency.
Serve hot, garnished with parsley; taste sauce and adjust salt and pepper to taste.
tip: Sub 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes for heat. Meatballs keep 4 days refrigerated; reheat gently in sauce. For baking: place on oiled sheet and bake at 400°F for 15–18 minutes to 165°F.

title: Turkey Tetrazzini
steps: Heat oven to 375°F. Grease a 2-quart baking dish. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook spaghetti until just shy of al dente, about 8 minutes; drain.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add mushrooms and onion; cook until mushrooms release liquid and brown, 8 to 10 minutes. Stir in garlic; cook 30 seconds.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables and cook, stirring, 1 minute. Whisk in broth, wine, and cream; simmer, stirring, until smooth and lightly thickened, 4 to 5 minutes.
Season sauce with salt and pepper. Stir in peas, turkey, half the Parmesan (1/4 cup), and cooked spaghetti until coated.
Transfer mixture to the prepared dish. In a small bowl, combine remaining Parmesan, breadcrumbs, and parsley; sprinkle evenly on top.
Bake at 375°F until bubbling at edges and topping is golden, 20 to 25 minutes. Let rest 5 minutes before serving to set the casserole.
tip: Substitute cooked chicken for turkey if needed. Assemble up to 1 day ahead; cover and refrigerate, then bake 30–35 minutes, tenting with foil if browning too quickly.

title: Duck à l'Orange
ing: 1 (5 lb) whole duck, giblets removed and patted dry
2 tbsp unsalted butter, cold and cubed
steps: Heat oven to 425°F. Prick duck skin all over (avoid meat). Season outside and cavity with 2 tsp salt and 1 tsp pepper. Tuck wingtips, place breast-side up on a rack in a roasting pan.
Roast at 425°F for 45 minutes. Carefully pour off fat. Reduce oven to 350°F and continue roasting until thighs reach 175°F and juices run clear, 35–45 minutes more. Rest duck 15 minutes on a board.

While duck roasts, make caramel: in a saucepan combine 2 tbsp sugar with 2 tbsp water; cook without stirring over medium heat until deep amber, 5–7 minutes. Carefully add 2 tbsp white wine vinegar; simmer 30 seconds.
Add 1/2 cup dry white wine and 1 cup chicken stock; simmer for 6 minutes. Add 1 cup fresh orange juice and 1 tbsp orange zest; simmer until reduced to about 1 1/4 cups, 10–12 minutes.
In a small bowl, mash 2 tbsp soft butter with 2 tbsp flour to make a beurre manié. Whisk pieces into the simmering sauce and cook until glossy and lightly thickened, 2–3 minutes.
Whisk in 2 tbsp Grand Marnier and a pinch of salt to taste. Keep warm on low. If desired, strain for a classic smooth finish.
Carve duck: remove legs and thighs, separate drumsticks and thighs, then slice breasts from the bone and cut crosswise into 1/2-inch slices.
Skim any fat from pan drippings, whisk drippings into orange sauce. Serve duck on warmed plates, spoon sauce over, and garnish with orange segments and 1 tbsp chopped parsley.
tip: Save rendered duck fat for roasting potatoes. Orange sauce can be made up to 2 days ahead; rewarm gently and whisk before serving.

title: Peking Duck
ing: 1 medium cucumber, cut into thin batons
steps: Trim excess fat from the duck and rinse; pat completely dry. Prick skin all over with a skewer, avoiding the meat. Mix honey, rice vinegar, and 1/2 cup boiling water; brush all over duck.
Air-dry the duck uncovered on a rack in the refrigerator for 12 to 24 hours until skin is taut and dry to the touch.
Remove duck 30 minutes before roasting. Preheat oven to 425°F. Season cavity lightly with salt and pepper. Place duck on a rack over a roasting pan, breast up.
Roast at 425°F for 25 minutes, then reduce to 350°F and continue roasting for 55 to 65 minutes, rotating pan once, until thickest part of thigh reaches 165°F. Rest 15 minutes.
While duck roasts, make pancakes: In a bowl combine flour and 3/4 cup boiling water; stir, then knead 5 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest 20 minutes. Roll into a 12-inch log, cut 12 pieces.

Brush each piece with a thin film of sesame oil. Pair pieces, oil sides facing; roll each pair into a 7-inch round. Heat a dry skillet over medium and cook each round 45 to 60 seconds per side until puffed.
Peel layers apart to make 12 thin pancakes. Keep warm wrapped in a towel. Mix hoisin with soy sauce and 1 tbsp water; set aside. Toss cucumbers and scallions; set aside.
Return duck to 425°F for 8 to 10 minutes to re-crisp skin. Carve: remove legs, wings, then slice breast thinly, separating crisp skin. Serve with pancakes, hoisin sauce, scallions, and cucumber.
Optionally render reserved duck fat: warm trimmed fat with 2 tbsp frying oil over low heat 20 minutes; strain for later use.
tip: Drying the duck overnight is key to crisp skin. Pancakes can be made 1 day ahead; reheat 5 minutes, covered, at 300°F or steam 2 minutes.

title: Crispy Duck Breast with Cherry Sauce
ing: 1 cup fresh or frozen pitted cherries
steps: Pat duck breasts dry, score skin in a 1/2-inch crosshatch without cutting meat, then season all over with 2 tsp salt and 1 tsp pepper. Let stand at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Set duck skin-side down in a cold skillet with 1 tsp frying oil. Cook over medium heat until fat renders and skin is deep golden and crisp, 10 to 12 minutes. Spoon off excess fat as needed.
Flip duck and cook meat-side down until medium-rare, 3 to 5 minutes, or to 135°F in the thickest part. Transfer to a warm plate, tent loosely with foil, and rest 8 minutes.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp duck fat. Add cherries, sugar, and vinegar; cook over medium heat, stirring, until cherries soften, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add red wine and kirsch; simmer for 3 minutes to reduce by about half. Stir in chicken stock and thyme; simmer for 4 to 5 minutes until slightly syrupy.
Whisk cornstarch with 1 tbsp cold water. Stir slurry into sauce; simmer 1 minute until glossy and lightly thickened. Off heat, whisk in butter and orange zest. Season to taste.
Slice rested duck crosswise into 1/4-inch slices. Spoon cherry sauce onto warm plates and fan duck over the sauce, skin-side up, to keep it crisp.
Serve immediately with any pan juices spooned over the sauce, not the skin, to preserve crispness.
tip: Substitute 1 cup good cherry jam for cherries and sugar; thin with stock. Rendered duck fat keeps 1 month refrigerated; use for potatoes. Cook duck to 165°F if you prefer well-done.

title: Duck Ragu with Pappardelle
steps: Pat duck legs dry, season with 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp pepper. Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat and brown duck, skin-side down first, 6–8 minutes per side until deep golden; remove.
Pour off all but 2 tbsp fat. Add onion, carrot, and celery; cook over medium heat, stirring, until softened and lightly golden, 8–10 minutes. Add garlic; cook 30 seconds.
Deglaze with 1/2 cup red wine, scraping browned bits; simmer 2 minutes. Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf; return duck to pot, skin side up.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook over low heat for 1 hour. Uncover and continue to simmer, turning occasionally, until duck is very tender and sauce thickens, 45–60 minutes.

Transfer duck to a board; discard skin if desired. Shred meat with forks, discarding bones. Return meat to pot; simmer 5 minutes. Stir in 1/2 cup whole milk; simmer 3 minutes. Adjust salt and pepper to taste.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook 12 oz pappardelle until al dente, 2–3 minutes for fresh or 8–10 minutes for dried; reserve 1/2 cup pasta water and drain.
Add pasta to ragu over low heat, tossing and loosening with splashes of reserved pasta water until glossy and well-coated, 1–2 minutes.
Serve hot in warm bowls, topped with 1/4 cup Parmesan and 2 tbsp chopped parsley.
tip: Make ahead: Ragu improves overnight; chill up to 3 days or freeze 2 months. Swap: Use duck confit legs; start at shredding step and simmer 15 minutes with tomatoes, stock, and wine to marry flavors.

title: Roasted Cornish Game Hens
ing: 4 Cornish game hens, 1 to 1 1/4 lb each
1 lemon, zested and cut into 8 wedges
2 tbsp fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish
steps: Pat hens dry and tuck wing tips. In a bowl mix butter, olive oil, 1 1/2 tsp salt, pepper, thyme, rosemary, and lemon zest to a paste.
Rub herb butter under breast skin and over hens. Stuff each cavity with 1 garlic clove and 2 lemon wedges. Tie legs loosely with kitchen twine.
Arrange hens breast-side up on a rack set over a roasting pan. Pour chicken broth and white wine into the pan below the rack.
Roast at 425°F for 25 minutes. Baste with pan juices, rotate the pan, and continue roasting 15 to 25 minutes until thickest thigh reaches 165°F; skin should be deep golden.
Transfer hens to a platter and tent loosely with foil to rest 10 minutes. Skim fat from pan juices and place pan over medium heat on stovetop.
Simmer pan juices for 3 to 5 minutes, scraping browned bits, until slightly syrupy. Adjust seasoning with a pinch of salt if needed.
Carve hens in half through the breastbone or serve whole. Spoon pan jus over and garnish with parsley and extra lemon wedges.
tip: Swap wine with more broth if preferred. Refrigerate leftovers up to 3 days; reheat, covered, at 325°F until warmed through.

title: Samgyetang
ing: 2 small chickens (Cornish hens), about 1.5 lb each, rinsed and patted dry
1/2 cup glutinous rice, rinsed and soaked 1 hour, drained
1 tbsp sesame seeds, toasted, for garnish
2 tbsp scallions, thinly sliced, for garnish
steps: Stuff each chicken with equal portions of soaked glutinous rice, 4 cloves garlic, 2 jujubes, half the ginseng, and 2 chestnuts. Close cavity with a skewer or tie legs to keep stuffing inside.
Place stuffed chickens breast-side up in a pot. Add 8 cups water, scallion pieces, ginger, 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp pepper. Bring to a boil over high heat, skimming foam, about 10 minutes.

Reduce to a gentle simmer, cover slightly ajar, and cook for 60 to 75 minutes until chickens are very tender and rice inside is fully cooked. Maintain a steady simmer; add hot water if needed to keep chickens submerged.
Check doneness: the thickest part of thigh must reach 165°F and juices run clear. Remove and discard scallion and ginger pieces.
Adjust seasoning in the broth with salt and pepper to taste. If desired, skim excess fat from the surface with a spoon for a cleaner broth.
Transfer each chicken to a bowl and ladle hot broth over. Split chickens gently to expose the stuffed rice without spilling it out.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and thinly sliced scallions. Serve immediately with small dishes of salt and pepper for dipping, and extra hot broth on the side.
tip: If fresh ginseng is unavailable, use 1 oz dried ginseng slices and simmer them in the broth. Leftovers keep 3 days refrigerated; reheat gently to avoid breaking the stuffed rice.
